birch@1.note: White bark, fine hanging twigs, pointed leaves and wind-borne seeds.

king-coconut@1.label: King coconut
king-coconut@1.note: A palm from a whole golden nut: whole first leaves, then a ringed trunk and a crown of arching fronds, cream flower spikes and bunches of golden-orange nuts.

layer.label: 1 · Canopy
layer.note: the tall trees over everything

stages.name: Seed nut
stages.note: The whole golden husked nut, laid on its side half sunk in moist soil: the seed of a palm is its fruit.

stages.name: Germination
stages.note: A pointed spike breaks out of the nut’s stem end, roots push down through the husk.

stages.name: Seedling
stages.note: The first leaves, whole and split only at their tip; the seedling still feeds on the nut.

stages.name: Young palm
stages.note: Its leaves start to split into leaflets; the nut beside it, spent, rots away.

stages.name: Juvenile
stages.note: A broad base, no trunk yet, a fountain of pinnate fronds two metres long.

stages.name: Flowering
stages.note: A grey trunk ringed with leaf scars; boat-shaped spathes split and the cream flower spikes open.

stages.name: Fruit set
stages.note: Green-gold buttons set on the branched spikes; many drop, the best hold on.

stages.name: Young nuts
stages.note: Bunches of bright golden-orange nuts, full of sweet water: the king coconut’s drinking stage.

stages.name: Maturing
stages.note: The nuts fill their shells with white meat, a new bunch every month above them.

stages.name: Ripe
stages.note: Heavy bunches dulling to orange-brown under a crown of thirty fronds; the palm keeps fruiting for decades.

mango@1.label: Mango
mango@1.note: From a flat stone to a dome as wide as it is tall: a short trunk, scaffold limbs at 45°, flush after flush breaking in whorls from each tip; bronze-red new leaves, panicles at the tips, mangoes on long stalks turning gold and red.

layer.label: 1 · Canopy
layer.note: the tall trees over everything

stages.name: Stone
stages.note: The flat fibrous stone, ten centimetres long, laid flat a few centimetres down, kept warm and moist.

stages.name: Germination
stages.note: A taproot dives; a hooked shoot comes up out of the stone — its seed leaves stay inside, feeding it.

stages.name: Seedling
stages.note: A whorl of limp bronze-red leaves at the shoot’s tip, greening as they firm: the first flush.

stages.name: Sapling
stages.note: A clear trunk, then three or four scaffold limbs at about 45° breaking from one ring of buds.

stages.name: Young tree
stages.note: Flush after flush: each tip breaks into two or three new shoots, the crown filling out into a dome.

stages.name: Flowering
stages.note: A dome as wide as tall; upright panicles of tiny pink-cream flowers at the shoot tips.

stages.name: Fruit set
stages.note: Most flowers fall; one or two small green fruit hold on each panicle.

stages.name: Green fruit
stages.note: Mangoes swelling on their long dangling stalks, green and hard; the next flush grows past them.

stages.name: Colouring
stages.note: They turn from green to gold, the sunny side blushing red.

stages.name: Ripe
stages.note: Ripe mangoes, golden and red, fragrant at the stalk: picking time.

durian@1.label: Durian
durian@1.note: A tall conical tree, its near-level limbs in tiers; clusters of cream flowers along the limbs, then heavy spiny fruit hanging from them.

layer.label: 1 · Canopy
layer.note: the tall trees over everything

stages.name: Seed
stages.note: A big glossy brown seed, four centimetres long, sown fresh — it dies if it dries.

stages.name: Germination
stages.note: A thick root goes down, the shoot comes up from between the fleshy halves.

stages.name: Seedling
stages.note: A slender stem, its leaves glossy green above, golden-brown and scaly beneath.

stages.name: Sapling
stages.note: A straight leader with its first level side limbs: a young cone.

stages.name: Young tree
stages.note: A tall conical tree, its limbs near level in tiers up the trunk; the lowest dying off.

stages.name: Flowering
stages.note: Clusters of big cream flowers hang along the limbs, opening at dusk for the bats.

stages.name: Fruit set
stages.note: A few flowers in each cluster set small green fruit, spiny from the start.

stages.name: Green fruit
stages.note: Heavy spiny fruit, as big as a head, hanging from the limbs on stout stalks.

stages.name: Ripening
stages.note: The spines turn from green to yellow-brown; the smell begins.

stages.name: Ripe
stages.note: Ripe durians, yellow-brown and fragrant, ready to fall in the night.

jackfruit@1.label: Jackfruit
jackfruit@1.note: One straight trunk under a dense dome of big glossy leaves; its flower heads and huge knobbly fruit come straight out of the trunk and the thickest limbs, the fruit hanging against the bark.

layer.label: 1 · Canopy
layer.note: the tall trees over everything

stages.name: Seed
stages.note: A pale brown seed three centimetres long, its slimy coat washed off, sown fresh.

stages.name: Germination
stages.note: A root goes down, the shoot comes up; the fleshy seed leaves stay inside the seed below.

stages.name: Seedling
stages.note: A slender green stem, its first leaves glossy and often two- or three-lobed; its sap white and sticky.

stages.name: Sapling
stages.note: A straight leader a metre tall, its leaves now whole, its first side limbs breaking.

stages.name: Young tree
stages.note: A cone of near-level limbs round one straight trunk, big glossy leaves crowded at the shoot tips.

stages.name: Flowering
stages.note: A dense dome over a clear trunk; short leafy footstalks burst from the bark with club-shaped green flower heads.

stages.name: Fruit set
stages.note: The male heads blacken and drop; the female heads swell into small knobbly green fruit, right on the bark.

stages.name: Green fruit
stages.note: Huge oblong fruit hanging straight down against the trunk, knobbly with short blunt spines.

stages.name: Ripening
stages.note: The skin yellows, the spines flatten; it smells sweet.

stages.name: Ripe
stages.note: Ripe jackfruit, up to half a metre long and tens of kilograms, in clusters all up the trunk and along the limbs.

safou@1.label: Safou
safou@1.note: A dense evergreen dome; panicles of small flowers at the tips, then clusters of oblong fruit turning from pink to deep blue-violet.

layer.label: 1 · Canopy
layer.note: the tall trees over everything

stages.name: Seed
stages.note: The big seed of a safou, sown fresh — it will not keep.

stages.name: Germination
stages.note: A root goes down; the shoot comes up from between the fleshy seed leaves.

stages.name: Seedling
stages.note: Its first leaves, compound, glossy.

stages.name: Sapling
stages.note: A slender young tree.

stages.name: Young tree
stages.note: A dense, rounded evergreen crown of glossy compound leaves.

stages.name: Flowering
stages.note: Panicles of small yellowish flowers at the shoot tips.

stages.name: Fruit set
stages.note: Small pink fruit set in clusters.

stages.name: Pink fruit
stages.note: Oblong fruit swelling, pink and pale.

stages.name: Colouring
stages.note: They darken through violet toward blue.

stages.name: Ripe
stages.note: Clusters of deep blue-violet safous, their green-cream flesh buttery: roast them.

sapodilla@1.label: Sapodilla
sapodilla@1.note: A dense evergreen pyramid, glossy leaves crowded in whorls at the shoot tips; small whitish bells, then round-oval fruit with a sandy brown scurfy skin.

layer.label: 1 · Canopy
layer.note: the tall trees over everything

stages.name: Seed
stages.note: A glossy black flattened seed with a white scar, a centimetre down.

stages.name: Germination
stages.note: Slow: a month before the root goes down and the hook comes up.

stages.name: Seedling
stages.note: Glossy leaves crowded at the tip of the shoot.

stages.name: Sapling
stages.note: A slow, symmetrical little tree, its sap a milky latex (chicle).

stages.name: Young tree
stages.note: A dense evergreen pyramid, its glossy leaves clustered at every shoot tip.

stages.name: Flowering
stages.note: Small bell-shaped whitish flowers among the leaves at the shoot tips.

stages.name: Fruit set
stages.note: Small rusty fruit set, a style sticking out of each tip.

stages.name: Growing
stages.note: Round-oval fruit with a sandy brown scurfy skin, growing slowly.

stages.name: Maturing
stages.note: Rub the scurf off: if the skin is no longer green beneath, it is ready to pick.

stages.name: Ripe
stages.note: Brown sapodillas — sapotilles — soft after picking, their flesh brown sugar and pear.

avocado@1.label: Avocado
avocado@1.note: From a big stone that splits open: a leggy stem, then strong limbs arching into a broad dome skirted to the ground; leaves crowded at the shoot tips, each flush bronze; panicles of tiny yellow-green flowers, and pear-shaped pebbly fruit hanging under the new leaves on long stalks.

layer.label: 1 · Canopy
layer.note: the tall trees over everything

stages.name: Stone
stages.note: The big avocado stone, five centimetres, set broad end down with its tip at the surface.

stages.name: Germination
stages.note: The stone splits from its base; a thick root goes down, a shoot comes up between the halves — the seed leaves stay inside the stone.

stages.name: Seedling
stages.note: A bare stem with little scale leaves, a tuft of big leaves at its top, bronze as they unfold.

stages.name: Sapling
stages.note: A leggy young tree, a cluster of leaves at the tip of each flush, its first limbs breaking.

stages.name: Young tree
stages.note: A spreading young tree on a short trunk, strong limbs arching out and over, leaves crowded at the shoot tips.

stages.name: Flowering
stages.note: Clusters of panicles at the shoot tips, hundreds of small yellow-green flowers each.

stages.name: Fruit set
stages.note: Of all those flowers a panicle keeps one, rarely two; the shoot grows on out of it in a bronze flush.

stages.name: Green fruit
stages.note: Pear-shaped avocados hanging under the new leaves on long stalks that thicken toward the fruit.

stages.name: Mature
stages.note: Full-sized, 8–10 cm, the pebbly Hass skin dull dark green; they keep on the tree and ripen only once picked.

stages.name: Late season
stages.note: Left on the tree, the sunny side of the skin turns purple-black; picked, they soften within a week.

walnut@1.label: Walnut
walnut@1.note: A broad dome on a clear grey trunk: long pinnate leaves bronze as they open, green catkins on last year’s wood, green husked walnuts in ones to threes at the shoot tips, splitting brown-black over the ripe nuts.

layer.label: 1 · Canopy
layer.note: the tall trees over everything

stages.name: Nut
stages.note: A walnut in its shell, sown in the autumn five centimetres down — where a jay or a squirrel would have buried it — and chilled by the winter.

stages.name: Germination
stages.note: In the spring the shell splits along its seam: a thick root goes straight down; the seed leaves stay in the shell.

stages.name: Seedling
stages.note: A stout shoot with its first leaves, already pinnate, bronze as they open; the taproot is longer than the shoot.

stages.name: Sapling
stages.note: A straight whip of smooth olive-grey bark, its big leaves in a tuft at the top; it leafs out late, after the frosts.

stages.name: Young tree
stages.note: A broad crown on a stout grey trunk, eight metres across in a forest garden at eight years, heading for twenty.

stages.name: Flowering
stages.note: In May with the bronze new leaves: green male catkins hanging from last year’s wood, and at the tips of the new shoots little green female flowers with two feathery stigmas.

stages.name: Nut set
stages.note: The catkins drop; at the shoot tips one to three small green fruits swell, smooth and dotted pale.

stages.name: Green walnuts
stages.note: Green husked walnuts the size of a hen’s egg at the shoot tips — picked now in June for nocino, before the shell hardens.

stages.name: Turning
stages.note: The husks yellow and spot with brown; inside, the shell has hardened and the kernel filled.

stages.name: Ripe
stages.note: The husks go brown-black and split; the wrinkled nuts show and drop — gather them quickly, before the squirrels.

chestnut@1.label: Sweet chestnut
chestnut@1.note: A big domed tree of long, bristle-toothed leaves; at midsummer long cream catkins all over the crown, then spiny green burrs at the shoot tips, fading yellow-brown and splitting over two or three glossy chestnuts.

layer.label: 1 · Canopy
layer.note: the tall trees over everything

stages.name: Nut
stages.note: A fresh chestnut, glossy brown, sown in the autumn before it dries out, four centimetres down.

stages.name: Germination
stages.note: In the spring a thick root pushes out of the pointed tip and down; the seed leaves stay in the nut.

stages.name: Seedling
stages.note: A straight shoot of long, toothed leaves, each tooth ending in a bristle.

stages.name: Sapling
stages.note: A fast young tree, its bark smooth and olive-grey, its leaves in two rows along the shoots.

stages.name: Young tree
stages.note: A broad dome on a stout trunk, its bark beginning to fissure — and to twist, in a spiral, as it ages.

stages.name: Flowering
stages.note: Late, at midsummer, in full leaf: long cream catkins stand out from the shoot tips by the hundred, heavy-scented; small green female flowers sit at the base of the upper ones.

stages.name: Burr set
stages.note: The catkins brown and fall; where the female flowers were, little green burrs bristle.

stages.name: Green burrs
stages.note: Spiny green burrs the size of a fist at the shoot tips, one to three nuts in each.

stages.name: Turning
stages.note: The burrs fade yellow-brown; the nuts inside harden and darken.

stages.name: Ripe
stages.note: The burrs split in four and gape: two or three glossy red-brown chestnuts in each, dropping in October.

alder@1.label: Black alder
alder@1.note: The support tree: a narrow cone on a straight dark trunk, round notched leaves, purple-brown catkins in late winter, little woody cones — and on its roots the orange nodules where Frankia fixes nitrogen for the garden.

layer.label: 1 · Canopy
layer.note: the tall trees over everything

stages.name: Seed
stages.note: A tiny flat nutlet with a narrow corky wing — alder seed floats down streams — on wet soil, barely covered.

stages.name: Germination
stages.note: A thread of a root, then a hook of a stem.

stages.name: Seedling
stages.note: Two small round seed leaves, then round toothed leaves; Frankia from the soil already swelling the first nodules on its roots.

stages.name: Sapling
stages.note: A slender, fast whip, a metre or more in its second year, its young leaves sticky (glutinosa).

stages.name: Young tree
stages.note: A narrow cone of a tree on one straight dark trunk, its limbs level in tiers: the support tree, its nodules feeding the garden nitrogen.

stages.name: Flowering
stages.note: In late winter, before the leaves: long purple-brown catkins at the twig tips loosening yellow with pollen; below them, tiny dark red female catkins.

stages.name: Cone set
stages.note: The leaves unfold, round and notched at the tip; the female catkins swell into little green cones.

stages.name: Green cones
stages.note: Clusters of green cones on short stalks, and next year’s catkins already formed, small and stiff.

stages.name: Turning
stages.note: The cones darken and harden, olive to brown.

stages.name: Ripe
stages.note: Dark woody cones, their scales open, shedding seed through the winter; the leaves fall green — alder keeps no autumn colour.

linden@1.label: Small-leaved lime
linden@1.note: A tall, dense crown of small heart-shaped leaves (the young ones good to eat); in July hanging clusters of pale yellow scented flowers on their leafy bracts, then little round nutlets that spin away on them.

layer.label: 1 · Canopy
layer.note: the tall trees over everything

stages.name: Nutlet
stages.note: A round grey felted nutlet, four ribs faint on it, sown in the autumn: it may lie a winter or two before it wakes.

stages.name: Germination
stages.note: The root goes down; the hook comes up.

stages.name: Seedling
stages.note: Two odd seed leaves, each cut into five fingers like a little hand, then the first heart-shaped leaves.

stages.name: Sapling
stages.note: A slim young tree, its zigzag shoots red-brown, its leaves in two rows along them.

stages.name: Young tree
stages.note: A tall, dense, egg-shaped crown on a grey trunk, deep shade under it; its soft young leaves are good to eat in a spring salad.

stages.name: Flowering
stages.note: In July, after the other limes: hanging clusters of pale yellow flowers, sweetly scented and loud with bees, each on a long stalk half-joined to a pale leafy bract.

stages.name: Fruit set
stages.note: The flowers fade; small green nutlets set in the clusters, the bracts still pale and fresh.

stages.name: Green nutlets
stages.note: Clusters of little round green nutlets hanging under the leaves on their bracts.

stages.name: Turning
stages.note: The nutlets felt over grey-brown; the bracts go papery and tan.

stages.name: Ripe
stages.note: Hard round nutlets, the bract a wing: in the autumn wind the whole cluster spins away.

pecan@1.label: Pecan
pecan@1.note: The finest nut of the canopy: a tall oval crown on a straight trunk, long arching pinnate leaves, green catkins in threes, then clusters of four-ridged green husks splitting over smooth, long brown pecans.

layer.label: 1 · Canopy
layer.note: the tall trees over everything

stages.name: Nut
stages.note: A pecan in its thin shell, soaked for two days and sown in the spring four centimetres down, after a winter in the cold.

stages.name: Germination
stages.note: A thick white root straight down; the seed leaves stay in the shell.

stages.name: Seedling
stages.note: A stout shoot with its first leaves, pinnate, the leaflets long and curved like a sickle.

stages.name: Sapling
stages.note: A straight young tree with a deep taproot, slow to leaf in the spring and its leaves long and arching.

stages.name: Young tree
stages.note: A tall, oval crown on a straight grey trunk, the bark breaking into narrow scaly ridges — heading for thirty metres.

stages.name: Flowering
stages.note: In late May with the leaves: green catkins hanging in threes from last year’s wood, and at the new shoot tips small spikes of female flowers.

stages.name: Nut set
stages.note: The catkins drop; at the shoot tips clusters of three to six small green nuts, each with four ridges.

stages.name: Green nuts
stages.note: Clusters of ridged green husks the size of a walnut, hanging at the ends of the shoots.

stages.name: Turning
stages.note: The husks darken to brown at their seams.

stages.name: Ripe
stages.note: The husks split along their four ridges and open: smooth brown pecans, long and pointed, dropping in October — the best of the nuts.

tree-hazel@1.label: Turkish tree hazel
tree-hazel@1.note: A hazel grown into a tall tree: one straight trunk with corky bark, a narrow pyramid of big dark leaves, yellow lamb’s tails in late winter, then hazelnuts by the cluster in long, curly fringed husks.

layer.label: 1 · Canopy
layer.note: the tall trees over everything

stages.name: Nut
stages.note: A thick-shelled hazelnut, sown in the autumn three centimetres down, chilled by the winter.

stages.name: Germination
stages.note: The shell cracks at its tip: the root goes down; the seed leaves stay in the nut.

stages.name: Seedling
stages.note: A single straight shoot of broad, double-toothed leaves — no suckers: this hazel is a tree.

stages.name: Sapling
stages.note: A neat young tree on one trunk, its crown a narrow cone; it shrugs off drought, heat and city air.

stages.name: Young tree
stages.note: A tall pyramid of a crown on a straight trunk with corky, flaking grey bark, its limbs level, the leaves big and dark.

stages.name: Flowering
stages.note: In late winter, before the leaves: long yellow lamb’s tails by the hundred, and the tiny crimson-tufted female flowers.

stages.name: Nut set
stages.note: The leaves come; at the shoot tips the nuts form in clusters of three to six, each wrapped in a long, deeply fringed husk.

stages.name: Green clusters
stages.note: Clusters of nuts in their curly green bracts, like little bunches of lettuce, all over the crown.

stages.name: Turning
stages.note: The husks dry and curl at their tips; the shells turn tan.

stages.name: Ripe
stages.note: Brown hazelnuts falling out of their dry fringed husks in September — the same sweet hazelnut, from a tree twenty metres tall.

korean-pine@1.label: Korean pine
korean-pine@1.note: The evergreen of the canopy and the hardiest nut pine: a tall cone of level tiers, soft blue-green needles in fives, and at the top of the crown fat upright cones that ripen over two summers and fall full of big sweet pine nuts.

layer.label: 1 · Canopy
layer.note: the tall trees over everything

stages.name: Seed
stages.note: A big wingless pine nut in its hard shell, soaked and chilled through the winter, sown in the spring two centimetres down.

stages.name: Germination
stages.note: The root goes down; the shoot comes up wearing the shell like a cap.

stages.name: Seedling
stages.note: A ring of a dozen slender seed leaves, then the first single needles.

stages.name: Sapling
stages.note: A small dense cone of soft blue-green needles in fives, slow for its first years, a whorl of branches a year.

stages.name: Young tree
stages.note: A tall cone of level tiers on one straight trunk, its bark grey-brown and scaly, its needles in long soft bundles.

stages.name: Flowering
stages.note: In June: clusters of yellow pollen cones at the base of the new shoots low in the crown; small red seed cones at the tips of the topmost shoots.

stages.name: Cone set
stages.note: The pollinated seed cones turn green and stop — a pine nut takes two summers to ripen.

stages.name: Green cones
stages.note: In the second summer the cones swell, upright at the top of the crown: green, fat, sticky with resin.

stages.name: Turning
stages.note: The cones go brown from their tips, their scales thick and woody.

stages.name: Ripe
stages.note: Big brown cones, their scales loosening on the big pine nuts — the sweet, rich nuts of the Siberian taiga, falling whole in the autumn.

apple@1.label: Apple
apple@1.note: From a pip to an open crown on scaffold limbs: toothed leaves, clusters of pink-budded white blossom, apples flushing red on the sunny side.

layer.label: 2 · Low trees
layer.note: the smaller trees under the canopy: fruit and nut trees, the big herbs that stand like them

stages.name: Pip
stages.note: A brown teardrop pip, chilled through the winter, a centimetre down.

stages.name: Germination
stages.note: The radicle goes down, the hook comes up; the seed leaves lift out of the soil.

stages.name: Seedling
stages.note: Two oval seed leaves and the first toothed true leaves.

stages.name: Sapling
stages.note: A slender red-brown whip, its oval leaves soft and downy beneath.

stages.name: Young tree
stages.note: A clear trunk, tiers of scaffold limbs and laterals along them; the first knobbly spurs, each a rosette of leaves.

stages.name: Blossom
stages.note: On every spur a rosette of young leaves and a cluster of five or six: deep pink buds, the king flower in the middle opening first, white flushed pink.

stages.name: Fruit set
stages.note: The petals fall; the king fruit and one or two others swell, the rest drop in the June drop.

stages.name: Green apples
stages.note: Hard green apples hanging on their short stalks among the leaves.

stages.name: Colouring
stages.note: The sunny side flushes red, the ground colour turns from green to yellow.

stages.name: Ripe
stages.note: Hundreds of red-striped apples in clusters, the laterals bowed under them; they come away with a lift and a twist.

orange@1.label: Orange
orange@1.note: A dense evergreen dome of glossy leaves, waxy white blossom heavy with scent, round fruit full-sized green before they turn orange.

layer.label: 2 · Low trees
layer.note: the smaller trees under the canopy: fruit and nut trees, the big herbs that stand like them

stages.name: Seed
stages.note: A pale ridged seed a centimetre long, fresh from the fruit, a centimetre down.

stages.name: Germination
stages.note: The root goes down; the shoot hooks up — its seed leaves stay below in the seed.

stages.name: Seedling
stages.note: The first glossy leaves, their stalks winged, smelling of orange when crushed.

stages.name: Sapling
stages.note: A bushy little tree, flush after flush of dark glossy leaves.

stages.name: Young tree
stages.note: A dense rounded crown on a short trunk, evergreen.

stages.name: Blossom
stages.note: Waxy white flowers in small clusters at the shoot tips, heavy with scent: orange blossom.

stages.name: Fruit set
stages.note: Little green fruit set; most drop, the strongest stay.

stages.name: Green fruit
stages.note: Round green oranges, full-sized long before they colour.

stages.name: Colouring
stages.note: In the cool of the season the green fades and the orange comes through.

stages.name: Ripe
stages.note: Deep orange fruit among dark leaves, sweet; they keep on the tree for weeks.

lemon@1.label: Lemon
lemon@1.note: An open, thorny little tree, its new leaves flushed purple, purple-budded white flowers, oval fruit with a nipple turning yellow from the tip.

layer.label: 2 · Low trees
layer.note: the smaller trees under the canopy: fruit and nut trees, the big herbs that stand like them

stages.name: Seed
stages.note: A pale pointed seed, fresh from the fruit, a centimetre down.

stages.name: Germination
stages.note: The root goes down; the shoot hooks up, its seed leaves staying in the seed.

stages.name: Seedling
stages.note: Glossy leaves, the newest flushed purple-red.

stages.name: Sapling
stages.note: An open, rangy little tree, a sharp thorn at every leaf.

stages.name: Young tree
stages.note: An irregular crown, flushing and flowering on and off all year.

stages.name: Blossom
stages.note: Purple-tinged buds opening white, sweet-scented, at the shoot tips.

stages.name: Fruit set
stages.note: Small dark-green lemons set below the falling petals.

stages.name: Green fruit
stages.note: Oval green lemons with a nipple at their tip, full-sized but sour.

stages.name: Colouring
stages.note: The green pales to yellow from the tip.

stages.name: Ripe
stages.note: Bright yellow lemons, fragrant, while the tree flowers again above them.

banana@1.label: Banana
banana@1.note: From a sucker: a pseudostem of rolled leaf sheaths, huge paddle leaves torn by the wind; the flower stalk bends over, purple bracts lift off hands of fingers curving up, the male bud hanging below.

layer.label: 2 · Low trees
layer.note: the smaller trees under the canopy: fruit and nut trees, the big herbs that stand like them

stages.name: Sucker
stages.note: A sword sucker cut from its mother’s corm, its narrow leaves upright, set in the soil.

stages.name: Rooting
stages.note: Thick white roots break from the corm; the first leaf unrolls.

stages.name: First leaves
stages.note: Narrow sword leaves, then broader ones, unrolling from the top one after the other.

stages.name: Young plant
stages.note: A pseudostem of rolled leaf sheaths, the leaves broad paddles now.

stages.name: Full grown
stages.note: Three metres of pseudostem, a crown of huge leaves torn into strips by the wind.

stages.name: Shooting
stages.note: The flower stalk pushes up through the pseudostem and bends over, a purple bud at its end.

stages.name: Hands
stages.note: Bract after bract lifts and falls, each baring a hand of small fingers that curve up toward the light.

stages.name: Filling
stages.note: The fingers fill out, green and angular; the male bud hangs on below.

stages.name: Colouring
stages.note: Full and rounded, the first hand yellowing.

stages.name: Ripe
stages.note: A heavy bunch of yellow bananas; beside it the next sucker is already a young plant.

red-banana@1.label: Red banana
red-banana@1.note: The banana’s red sister: its pseudostem, leaf stalks and midribs flushed red-purple, short thick fingers ripening maroon to a dusky purple-red.

layer.label: 2 · Low trees
layer.note: the smaller trees under the canopy: fruit and nut trees, the big herbs that stand like them

stages.name: Sucker
stages.note: A red sucker cut from its mother’s corm, its narrow leaves upright, set in the soil.

stages.name: Rooting
stages.note: Thick white roots break from the corm; the first leaf unrolls.

stages.name: First leaves
stages.note: Narrow sword leaves, then broader ones, unrolling from the top one after the other.

stages.name: Young plant
stages.note: A pseudostem of rolled sheaths, flushed red-purple; red leaf stalks and midribs.

stages.name: Full grown
stages.note: Three metres of dark red pseudostem, a crown of huge leaves with red midribs, torn by the wind.

stages.name: Shooting
stages.note: The flower stalk pushes up through the pseudostem and bends over, a purple bud at its end.

stages.name: Hands
stages.note: Bract after bract lifts, baring hands of short thick fingers, maroon from the start.

stages.name: Filling
stages.note: The fingers fill out, plump and dark red.

stages.name: Colouring
stages.note: Full and rounded, the maroon lightening toward a dusky purple-red.

stages.name: Ripe
stages.note: A heavy bunch of red bananas, sweet with a hint of raspberry; beside it the next sucker.

papaya@1.label: Papaya
papaya@1.note: One unbranched scarred stem, a crown of huge palmate leaves on long hollow stalks; cream flowers and then a ring of papayas hugging the stem in the leaf axils, ripening from below.

layer.label: 2 · Low trees
layer.note: the smaller trees under the canopy: fruit and nut trees, the big herbs that stand like them

stages.name: Seed
stages.note: A small black wrinkled seed in its clear jelly, washed, a centimetre down in warm soil.

stages.name: Germination
stages.note: The radicle goes down, the hook comes up.

stages.name: Seed leaves
stages.note: Two oval seed leaves, then a first small lobed leaf.

stages.name: Seedling
stages.note: A soft green stem, its leaves already deeply lobed.

stages.name: Young papaya
stages.note: One unbranched hollow stem, scarred where old leaves fell, a crown of huge palmate leaves on long hollow stalks.

stages.name: Flowering
stages.note: Waxy cream flowers in the axils of the leaves, right on the stem.

stages.name: Fruit set
stages.note: Small green fruit set close against the stem, one at each leaf axil.

stages.name: Green fruit
stages.note: A ring of heavy green papayas hugging the stem under the leaves, more forming above.

stages.name: Colouring
stages.note: The lowest turn yellow from their tips.

stages.name: Ripe
stages.note: Yellow-orange papayas below, green ones above: it fruits on as the stem grows.

soursop@1.label: Soursop
soursop@1.note: A small glossy-leaved tree; thick yellow-green flowers straight out of its limbs, then big heart-shaped fruit covered in soft curved spines.

layer.label: 2 · Low trees
layer.note: the smaller trees under the canopy: fruit and nut trees, the big herbs that stand like them

stages.name: Seed
stages.note: A glossy black seed from the pulp, a centimetre down.

stages.name: Germination
stages.note: A root goes down, the hook comes up.

stages.name: Seedling
stages.note: Glossy dark leaves, aromatic when crushed.

stages.name: Sapling
stages.note: A slender, upright little tree.

stages.name: Young tree
stages.note: A small tree, its limbs low, dense with glossy leaves.

stages.name: Flowering
stages.note: Thick fleshy yellow-green flowers, three big petals over three small, straight out of the limbs.

stages.name: Fruit set
stages.note: Small green fruit with soft curved spines.

stages.name: Green fruit
stages.note: Big heart-shaped soursops hanging from the limbs, spiny all over.

stages.name: Ripening
stages.note: The spines spread apart, the green dulls and yellows a little.

stages.name: Ripe
stages.note: Soft to a thumb: white custard flesh, sweet and sour — corossol.

cherry@1.label: Cherry
cherry@1.note: A tall steep crown; white blossom in clusters on the spurs, glossy cherries in pairs on long stalks, yellow to red to dark red.

layer.label: 2 · Low trees
layer.note: the smaller trees under the canopy: fruit and nut trees, the big herbs that stand like them

stages.name: Stone
stages.note: A cherry stone, chilled through the winter, three centimetres down.

stages.name: Germination
stages.note: The stone cracks along its seam; the root goes down, the hook comes up.

stages.name: Seedling
stages.note: Two fleshy seed leaves, then toothed true leaves, the stem reddish.

stages.name: Sapling
stages.note: A straight leader, its side shoots in tiers.

stages.name: Young tree
stages.note: A tall, steep crown; short fruiting spurs on the thin outer branches.

stages.name: Blossom
stages.note: Clusters of white blossom on long stalks hang from every spur.

stages.name: Fruit set
stages.note: The petals snow down; little green cherries in pairs and threes.

stages.name: Green cherries
stages.note: Hard green cherries swelling on their long stalks.

stages.name: Colouring
stages.note: Yellow, then blushing, then red.

stages.name: Ripe
stages.note: Glossy dark red cherries hanging in pairs: picking time, before the birds.

pear@1.label: Pear
pear@1.note: An upright narrow crown; white blossom with dark red anthers, pears narrow at the stalk and round below, yellowing with a russet cheek.

layer.label: 2 · Low trees
layer.note: the smaller trees under the canopy: fruit and nut trees, the big herbs that stand like them

stages.name: Pip
stages.note: A black teardrop pip, chilled through the winter, a centimetre down.

stages.name: Germination
stages.note: The radicle goes down, the seed leaves lift out of the soil.

stages.name: Seedling
stages.note: Two oval seed leaves and the first glossy true leaves.

stages.name: Sapling
stages.note: An upright whip, its branches steep.

stages.name: Young tree
stages.note: A tall narrow crown, spurs on its outer branches.

stages.name: Blossom
stages.note: White blossom with dark red anthers in clusters, early in the spring.

stages.name: Fruit set
stages.note: Little green pears on their stalks, the calyx still on their tips.

stages.name: Green pears
stages.note: The pears lengthen and fill, narrow at the stalk, broad below.

stages.name: Colouring
stages.note: Green turns to yellow, a russet blush on the sunny side.

stages.name: Ripe
stages.note: Yellow pears with a red cheek: picked hard, they soften indoors.

peach@1.label: Peach
peach@1.note: An open vase on three or four limbs, long narrow leaves, pink blossom; fuzzy peaches with a suture, yellow blushing red.

layer.label: 2 · Low trees
layer.note: the smaller trees under the canopy: fruit and nut trees, the big herbs that stand like them

stages.name: Stone
stages.note: A deeply pitted peach stone, chilled through the winter, five centimetres down.

stages.name: Germination
stages.note: The stone splits; a root goes down, a shoot comes up.

stages.name: Seedling
stages.note: Long narrow leaves on a reddish stem.

stages.name: Sapling
stages.note: Fast: a metre in its first year.

stages.name: Young tree
stages.note: Opened into a vase on three or four limbs, the middle kept open to the sun.

stages.name: Blossom
stages.note: Pink blossom all along last year’s shoots, before the leaves.

stages.name: Fruit set
stages.note: Fuzzy green peaches set below the falling petals.

stages.name: Green peaches
stages.note: The peaches swell, their suture showing, still green and hard.

stages.name: Colouring
stages.note: The ground colour turns yellow; a red blush spreads from the sunny side.

stages.name: Ripe
stages.note: Soft, fragrant, yellow and red under their fuzz.

apricot@1.label: Apricot
apricot@1.note: An open spreading crown, round pointed leaves; white blossom blushed pink, velvety orange apricots freckled red.

layer.label: 2 · Low trees
layer.note: the smaller trees under the canopy: fruit and nut trees, the big herbs that stand like them

stages.name: Stone
stages.note: A smooth flat apricot stone, chilled through the winter, four centimetres down.

stages.name: Germination
stages.note: The stone splits along its edge; the root goes down.

stages.name: Seedling
stages.note: Round, pointed leaves on long reddish stalks.

stages.name: Sapling
stages.note: A young tree, its bark reddish.

stages.name: Young tree
stages.note: An open, spreading crown, spurs on its outer branches.

stages.name: Blossom
stages.note: White blossom blushed pink, the very first of the year.

stages.name: Fruit set
stages.note: Small velvety green apricots set.

stages.name: Green apricots
stages.note: They fill out, their suture showing.

stages.name: Colouring
stages.note: Yellow-orange, freckled red on the sunny side.

stages.name: Ripe
stages.note: Orange apricots, soft and sweet, falling at a touch.

plum@1.label: Plum
plum@1.note: A rounded crown, knobbly with spurs; white blossom in pairs, oval plums with a suture turning blue-black under a pale bloom.

layer.label: 2 · Low trees
layer.note: the smaller trees under the canopy: fruit and nut trees, the big herbs that stand like them

stages.name: Stone
stages.note: A pointed Zwetschge stone, chilled through the winter, three centimetres down.

stages.name: Germination
stages.note: The stone splits; the root goes down.

stages.name: Seedling
stages.note: Toothed oval leaves on a downy stem.

stages.name: Sapling
stages.note: A young tree, its shoots grey-brown.

stages.name: Young tree
stages.note: A rounded crown, its outer branches knobbly with spurs.

stages.name: Blossom
stages.note: White blossom in pairs, smothering the spurs.

stages.name: Fruit set
stages.note: Little green plums set.

stages.name: Green plums
stages.note: Oval green plums, their suture down one side.

stages.name: Colouring
stages.note: They turn purple, then blue-black under a pale bloom.

stages.name: Ripe
stages.note: Blue Zwetschgen, the stone coming clean from the yellow flesh: Zwetschgendatschi time.

persimmon@1.label: Persimmon
persimmon@1.note: A rounded crown of big glossy leaves; pale bell flowers in the leaf axils, glossy orange fruit in four-lobed calyxes that hang on like lanterns after the leaves fall.

layer.label: 2 · Low trees
layer.note: the smaller trees under the canopy: fruit and nut trees, the big herbs that stand like them

stages.name: Seed
stages.note: A flat brown seed from a ripe kaki, chilled through the winter, two centimetres down.

stages.name: Germination
stages.note: Slow: a thick root goes down first, then the hook comes up.

stages.name: Seedling
stages.note: Two leathery seed leaves, then broad glossy true leaves.

stages.name: Sapling
stages.note: A slender young tree, its bark already chequered.

stages.name: Young tree
stages.note: A rounded crown of big, glossy, leathery leaves.

stages.name: Flowering
stages.note: Small pale-yellow bell flowers, one in each leaf axil of the new shoots, under a big green calyx.

stages.name: Fruit set
stages.note: The bells drop; little green fruit sit in their four-lobed calyxes.

stages.name: Green fruit
stages.note: Round green fruit swelling among the leaves.

stages.name: Colouring
stages.note: They turn yellow, then orange, as the leaves turn scarlet.

stages.name: Ripe
stages.note: Glossy orange kaki like lanterns; they hang on even after the leaves have fallen.

mulberry@1.label: Mulberry
mulberry@1.note: A broad spreading crown of toothed, often lobed leaves; green catkins, then berries like long blackberries going white, red, black, for weeks.

layer.label: 2 · Low trees
layer.note: the smaller trees under the canopy: fruit and nut trees, the big herbs that stand like them

stages.name: Seed
stages.note: A tiny seed from a berry, sown on the surface.

stages.name: Germination
stages.note: The radicle goes down, the hook comes up.

stages.name: Seedling
stages.note: Two small seed leaves, then toothed, heart-shaped leaves.

stages.name: Sapling
stages.note: Fast: a branching young tree, some leaves lobed, some whole.

stages.name: Young tree
stages.note: A broad, spreading, rounded crown.

stages.name: Flowering
stages.note: Small green catkins hang among the new leaves in spring.

stages.name: Fruit set
stages.note: The catkins swell into little green berries along their length.

stages.name: Green berries
stages.note: Clusters of hard green mulberries, like small blackberries.

stages.name: Colouring
stages.note: They go white, then red, berry by berry.

stages.name: Ripe
stages.note: Black mulberries, soft and juicy, ripening for weeks: the ground under the tree stained purple.

fig@1.label: Fig
fig@1.note: A low, many-stemmed tree of big rough hand-shaped leaves; its flowers hidden inside the figs, one in each leaf axil, pear-shaped, ripening purple.

layer.label: 2 · Low trees
layer.note: the smaller trees under the canopy: fruit and nut trees, the big herbs that stand like them

stages.name: Seed
stages.note: A tiny seed from a fig — though most figs are grown from cuttings, pushed into the soil in spring.

stages.name: Germination
stages.note: The radicle goes down, the hook comes up.

stages.name: Seedling
stages.note: Small seed leaves, then rough, lobed leaves.

stages.name: Sapling
stages.note: Thick grey shoots, big lobed leaves, the milky sap in every cut.

stages.name: Young tree
stages.note: A low, spreading, many-stemmed tree of big hand-shaped leaves, rough as sandpaper.

stages.name: Breba
stages.note: Early figs (brebas) swell on last year’s wood; the flowers are hidden inside them.

stages.name: Fruit set
stages.note: New little green figs in the leaf axils of this year’s shoots, one to each leaf.

stages.name: Green figs
stages.note: Pear-shaped green figs, swelling slowly, hard.

stages.name: Colouring
stages.note: They swell suddenly, soften and darken to purple, their eye at the tip opening.

stages.name: Ripe
stages.note: Soft purple figs hanging on their necks, a drop of nectar at the eye: picking time.

pomegranate@1.label: Pomegranate
pomegranate@1.note: A small tree of many stems, twiggy, its narrow glossy leaves bronze when new; scarlet trumpets at the shoot tips, then round leathery fruit under a crown, yellow flushing red.

layer.label: 2 · Low trees
layer.note: the smaller trees under the canopy: fruit and nut trees, the big herbs that stand like them

stages.name: Seed
stages.note: A small angular seed from an aril, its juicy red coat washed off, a centimetre down.

stages.name: Germination
stages.note: The radicle goes down, the hook comes up.

stages.name: Seedling
stages.note: Two small round seed leaves, then narrow glossy leaves in pairs on a reddish stem.

stages.name: Sapling
stages.note: Shoot after shoot from the base: a twiggy little bush, a few twigs ending in a thorn.

stages.name: Young tree
stages.note: A small tree of several stems, three metres high; narrow glossy leaves, bronze when new.

stages.name: Flowering
stages.note: Scarlet trumpets at the shoot tips: a fleshy red calyx and crumpled petals round a boss of yellow stamens.

stages.name: Fruit set
stages.note: The petals fall; the calyx swells into a little round fruit, still crowned with its lobes.

stages.name: Green fruit
stages.note: Round green fruit the size of a fist, heavy on the bending twigs.

stages.name: Colouring
stages.note: The skin turns yellow, then flushes red from the sunny side.

stages.name: Ripe
stages.note: Leathery red pomegranates under their crowns: inside, hundreds of seeds in ruby arils.

olive@1.label: Olive
olive@1.note: A gnarled grey trunk under a dome of narrow silvery leaves; sprays of tiny cream flowers in the leaf axils of last year’s shoots, olives ripening green, violet, black.

layer.label: 2 · Low trees
layer.note: the smaller trees under the canopy: fruit and nut trees, the big herbs that stand like them

stages.name: Stone
stages.note: A hard ridged olive stone, its flesh rotted off, two centimetres down: slow and fickle — most olives are grown from cuttings.

stages.name: Germination
stages.note: Weeks later the stone splits; the root goes down, the hook comes up.

stages.name: Seedling
stages.note: Two narrow seed leaves, then grey-green leaves in pairs.

stages.name: Sapling
stages.note: A slender young tree, silvery, its bark smooth and grey.

stages.name: Young tree
stages.note: A round crown of narrow silvery leaves on a trunk already twisting.

stages.name: Flowering
stages.note: Short sprays of tiny creamy flowers in the leaf axils of last year’s shoots, smelling of honey.

stages.name: Fruit set
stages.note: Most flowers fall; a few little green olives hold, one to three a spray.

stages.name: Green olives
stages.note: Firm green olives filling out among the leaves: picked now for green olives.

stages.name: Turning
stages.note: They turn straw-coloured, then blush violet from the tip.

stages.name: Ripe
stages.note: Purple-black olives, glossy, at the crown’s edge: picked now for oil.

cacao@1.label: Cacao
cacao@1.note: A stem to its jorquette, then a fan of level branches hung with big limp leaves, red when new; tiny pink-white flowers and big ridged pods straight out of the trunk and thick limbs.

layer.label: 2 · Low trees
layer.note: the smaller trees under the canopy: fruit and nut trees, the big herbs that stand like them

stages.name: Bean
stages.note: A fresh cacao bean from a split pod, still sticky with pulp, sown at once in the shade — it dies if it dries.

stages.name: Germination
stages.note: The root goes down; the thick seed leaves are lifted out of the soil.

stages.name: Seedling
stages.note: Long, soft, drooping leaves, pink-red as they unfold.

stages.name: Sapling
stages.note: One straight stem with its leaves in a spiral, a metre and a half high.

stages.name: Young tree
stages.note: At the jorquette the stem fans out into four or five level branches; flush after flush of limp red leaves.

stages.name: Flowering
stages.note: Cushions of tiny pink-white flowers straight out of the bark of the trunk and the thick limbs, pollinated by midges.

stages.name: Fruit set
stages.note: A few in a hundred set: little green pods (cherelles) on the trunk.

stages.name: Green pods
stages.note: Big ridged pods hanging from the trunk and the limbs, growing for months.

stages.name: Colouring
stages.note: The furrows yellow first, then the ridges: green to yellow to orange.

stages.name: Ripe
stages.note: Heavy yellow-orange pods rattling with beans in their white pulp: cut, split, ferment, dry.

cacao@2.label: Cacao
cacao@2.note: A stem to its jorquette, then a fan of level branches hung with big limp leaves, red when new; tiny pink-white flowers and big ridged pods straight out of the trunk and thick limbs.

layer.label: 2 · Low trees
layer.note: the smaller trees under the canopy: fruit and nut trees, the big herbs that stand like them

stages.name: Bean
stages.note: A fresh cacao bean from a split pod, still sticky with pulp, sown at once in the shade — it dies if it dries.

stages.name: Germination
stages.note: The root goes down; the thick seed leaves are lifted out of the soil.

stages.name: Seedling
stages.note: Long, soft, drooping leaves, pink-red as they unfold.

stages.name: Sapling
stages.note: One straight stem with its leaves in a spiral, a metre and a half high.

stages.name: Young tree
stages.note: At the jorquette the stem fans out into four or five level branches; flush after flush of limp red leaves.

stages.name: Flowering
stages.note: Cushions of tiny pink-white flowers straight out of the bark of the trunk and the thick limbs, pollinated by midges.

stages.name: Fruit set
stages.note: A few in a hundred set: little green pods (cherelles) on the trunk.

stages.name: Green pods
stages.note: Big ridged pods hanging from the trunk and the limbs, growing for months.

stages.name: Colouring
stages.note: The furrows yellow first, then the ridges: green to yellow to orange.

stages.name: Ripe
stages.note: Heavy yellow-orange pods rattling with beans in their white pulp: cut, split, ferment, dry.

hazel@1.label: Hazel
hazel@1.note: A coppice stool of straight stems from the base, round toothed leaves; yellow lamb’s tails and crimson-tufted female flowers on the bare twigs in late winter, then nuts in clusters in their frilly husks, ripening brown.

layer.label: 2 · Low trees
layer.note: the smaller trees under the canopy: fruit and nut trees, the big herbs that stand like them

stages.name: Nut
stages.note: A hazelnut in its shell, sown in the autumn three centimetres down, chilled by the winter.

stages.name: Germination
stages.note: The shell cracks at its tip: the root goes down; the seed leaves stay in the nut.

stages.name: Seedling
stages.note: A downy shoot of round, toothed, soft leaves.

stages.name: Sapling
stages.note: New stems come up from the base beside the first: the hazel is becoming a stool.

stages.name: Young stool
stages.note: Five to ten straight stems from the stool, four to six metres, cut every seven years or so for poles and grown again.

stages.name: Flowering
stages.note: In late winter, on the bare twigs: yellow lamb’s-tail catkins dangling in ones to fours, and tiny bud-like female flowers with tufts of crimson stigmas.

stages.name: Nut set
stages.note: The leaves come; where the red tufts were, tiny nuts form in clusters, each in a green frilly husk.

stages.name: Green nuts
stages.note: Clusters of green-white nuts in their ragged husks — and next year’s catkins already there, small, stiff and grey-green.

stages.name: Turning
stages.note: The husks dry at their edges; the shells turn from green-white to tan.

stages.name: Ripe
stages.note: Brown hazelnuts loose in browning husks, falling at a shake — before the squirrels and the dormice.

quince@1.label: Quince
quince@1.note: A small crooked tree of round felted leaves; one big pale-pink flower at the tip of each short new shoot, then a big downy fruit, pear- or apple-shaped, ripening golden.

layer.label: 2 · Low trees
layer.note: the smaller trees under the canopy: fruit and nut trees, the big herbs that stand like them

stages.name: Pip
stages.note: A brown quince pip, its coat turning to slime when wet, chilled through the winter, a centimetre down.

stages.name: Germination
stages.note: The radicle goes down; the hook comes up and lifts its seed leaves.

stages.name: Seedling
stages.note: Two oval seed leaves, then round true leaves, woolly underneath.

stages.name: Sapling
stages.note: A twiggy young tree, its shoots felted grey, already leaning its own way.

stages.name: Young tree
stages.note: A small crooked tree of four metres, low-branched, its round felted leaves dense.

stages.name: Blossom
stages.note: Late in the spring, one big pale-pink flower at the tip of each short new shoot, among the leaves.

stages.name: Fruit set
stages.note: The petals fall; a woolly green fruit swells under the five leafy sepals.

stages.name: Green quinces
stages.note: Big hard grey-green fruit, still in their grey felt, weighing the shoots down.

stages.name: Colouring
stages.note: The felt rubs off; they turn lemon-yellow, and the tree smells of them.

stages.name: Ripe
stages.note: Big golden quinces, lumpy, pear- or apple-shaped: rock hard, for jelly, paste and the cellar.

medlar@1.label: Medlar
medlar@1.note: A small spreading tree of long narrow leaves; big single white flowers at the shoot tips, then brown russet fruit, each with an open eye ringed by five long sepals.

layer.label: 2 · Low trees
layer.note: the smaller trees under the canopy: fruit and nut trees, the big herbs that stand like them

stages.name: Stone
stages.note: One of the five hard stones of a medlar, chilled through two winters, two centimetres down: slow and fickle — most are grafted.

stages.name: Germination
stages.note: In its second spring the stone splits; the root goes down, the seed leaves come up.

stages.name: Seedling
stages.note: Two oval seed leaves, then long narrow downy leaves.

stages.name: Sapling
stages.note: A slender young tree, its shoots downy, a few thorns on a wild one.

stages.name: Young tree
stages.note: A small tree as wide as it is high, its branches crooked and spreading level.

stages.name: Blossom
stages.note: In late spring, one big white flower at the tip of each short leafy shoot, its long sepals between the petals.

stages.name: Fruit set
stages.note: The petals fall; the sepals stay, round a green fruit already open at its end.

stages.name: Green medlars
stages.note: Round green-brown fruit, flattened, each with its open eye and five long sepals.

stages.name: Russeting
stages.note: They turn russet brown, rough and hard.

stages.name: Ripe
stages.note: Brown russet medlars picked hard after the first frost; laid down, they blet soft and brown, like apple sauce.

serviceberry@1.label: Serviceberry
serviceberry@1.note: A small tree of many grey stems: clouds of white starry flowers in racemes as its bronze leaves unfold, then hanging clusters of berries, red, then purple-black.

layer.label: 2 · Low trees
layer.note: the smaller trees under the canopy: fruit and nut trees, the big herbs that stand like them

stages.name: Seed
stages.note: A tiny brown seed from a berry, chilled through the winter, barely covered.

stages.name: Germination
stages.note: A root goes down, a tiny hook comes up.

stages.name: Seedling
stages.note: Two round seed leaves, then small oval toothed leaves, bronze as they unfold.

stages.name: Young bush
stages.note: Thin stems from the base, grey and smooth, the tallest above your head.

stages.name: Young tree
stages.note: A small tree of many grey stems, four metres high, its crown light and airy.

stages.name: Blossom
stages.note: Early in the spring, as the bronze leaves unfold: clouds of white stars in loose racemes at every shoot tip.

stages.name: Fruit set
stages.note: The petals fall; little green berries along the racemes, each crowned by its sepals.

stages.name: Green berries
stages.note: Clusters of green berries hanging, swelling, the leaves green now.

stages.name: Colouring
stages.note: In June they turn red, then berry by berry purple.

stages.name: Ripe
stages.note: Hanging clusters of red and purple-black berries, sweet, tasting of almond: the blackbirds know. In autumn the leaves turn orange and red.

cornel@1.label: Cornelian cherry
cornel@1.note: A dense small tree of opposite oval leaves with curving veins; tiny yellow umbels all over its bare twigs in late winter, glossy oval red cherries hanging along them in late summer.

layer.label: 2 · Low trees
layer.note: the smaller trees under the canopy: fruit and nut trees, the big herbs that stand like them

stages.name: Stone
stages.note: An oblong ribbed stone from a cornel cherry, two centimetres down: it lies two winters before it wakes.

stages.name: Germination
stages.note: In its second spring the root goes down and the seed leaves come up.

stages.name: Seedling
stages.note: Two oval seed leaves, then true leaves in opposite pairs, their veins curving to the tip.

stages.name: Sapling
stages.note: A slow, upright little tree, its twigs in pairs.

stages.name: Young tree
stages.note: A dense small tree of five metres, branching in pairs, leafy to the ground.

stages.name: Blossom
stages.note: In February, on the bare twigs: tiny yellow flowers in little umbels at every pair of buds, the whole tree a yellow haze.

stages.name: Fruit set
stages.note: The opposite oval leaves unfold after the flowers; a few small green fruit hold in each umbel.

stages.name: Green fruit
stages.note: Hard green oval fruit hanging in ones and twos all along the twigs.

stages.name: Colouring
stages.note: Through yellow and scarlet in August.

stages.name: Ripe
stages.note: Glossy oval cherries, dark red, sour until they fall: Kornelkirschen for jam, syrup and the schnapps.

pawpaw@1.label: Pawpaw
pawpaw@1.note: A small pyramidal tree of great drooping leaves; nodding maroon bells on last year’s wood, then clusters of green kidney-shaped fruit, custard inside.

layer.label: 2 · Low trees
layer.note: the smaller trees under the canopy: fruit and nut trees, the big herbs that stand like them

stages.name: Seed
stages.note: A big flat brown seed from a pawpaw, never dried, chilled through the winter, two centimetres down.

stages.name: Germination
stages.note: Slow: the root goes deep first; the seed leaves stay in the seed below the soil.

stages.name: Seedling
stages.note: A shoot with its first long leaves, wanting shade its first years.

stages.name: Sapling
stages.note: A slender young tree, its leaves big and drooping, its limbs in tiers.

stages.name: Young tree
stages.note: A narrow pyramid four metres high, its great drooping leaves hanging in layers, tropical-looking.

stages.name: Flowering
stages.note: In spring, as the leaves unfold: nodding maroon bells, three-petalled twice, on last year’s bare wood, smelling faintly of yeast.

stages.name: Fruit set
stages.note: Several fruit from each flower: little green clusters, like tiny bananas.

stages.name: Green fruit
stages.note: Clusters of two to four green fruit, kidney-shaped, swelling under the leaves.

stages.name: Colouring
stages.note: The green pales toward yellow; the fruit softens.

stages.name: Ripe
stages.note: Soft yellow-green pawpaws freckled brown, smelling of mango and banana: custard inside, big brown seeds.

bamboo@1.label: Bamboo
bamboo@1.note: A running clump from a piece of rhizome: every spring fat spotted shoots telescope up into ringed green culms, taller each year to six or eight metres, two branches at a node and fans of narrow leaves.

layer.label: 2 · Low trees
layer.note: the smaller trees under the canopy: fruit and nut trees, the big herbs that stand like them

stages.name: Rhizome
stages.note: A piece of running rhizome, jointed and yellowish with fat buds at its nodes, laid a hand deep in spring.

stages.name: First shoot
stages.note: A bud wakes: a thin shoot in papery sheaths pushes up and telescopes into a culm.

stages.name: First culms
stages.note: A few thin culms a metre or two high, ringed at every node, two branches at a node and fans of narrow leaves.

stages.name: Second year
stages.note: The rhizomes run out under the soil; new culms come up taller and thicker than the last.

stages.name: Spring shoots
stages.note: Its third spring: fat conical shoots in brown spotted sheaths break the soil all round — dug at a hand high, they are eaten.

stages.name: Culm extension
stages.note: Each shoot telescopes up, metres in a few weeks, its sheaths loosening and dropping as the nodes part.

stages.name: Leafing out
stages.note: The new culms branch at their nodes and leaf out in fans; under the soil the rhizomes run again.

stages.name: Grove
stages.note: Its fourth spring: the tallest culms yet shoot up through the clump, five to six metres of them.

stages.name: Mature grove
stages.note: A grove six to eight metres high, the tops arching under their leaves; the older culms dull and yellowing.

stages.name: Harvest
stages.note: The oldest culms cut at the ground for canes, the stand thinned; some leaves yellow in the spring leaf change.

raspberry@1.label: Raspberry
raspberry@1.note: From a pitted seed to a prickly cane, leafy its first summer; its second, side shoots of small white flowers and clusters of red raspberries, new canes and a sucker beside it.

layer.label: 3 · Shrubs
layer.note: the bushes: berries, woody herbs

stages.name: Seed
stages.note: A brown pitted seed two and a half millimetres long, chilled through the winter, a few millimetres down.

stages.name: Germination
stages.note: The radicle goes down, the hypocotyl hooks up toward the light.

stages.name: Seed leaves
stages.note: Two small round cotyledons on a short stem.

stages.name: True leaves
stages.note: The first toothed leaves, three leaflets each, white-felted beneath.

stages.name: First cane
stages.note: The primocane: a metre of green, red-flushed cane, prickly, five-leafleted leaves all the way up.

stages.name: Flowering
stages.note: Its second spring: the cane gone brown sends out side shoots with small white flowers; new canes rise beside it.

stages.name: Fruit set
stages.note: The petals drop; each flower’s pistils swell into a little green cluster of drupelets.

stages.name: Green berries
stages.note: Hard green berries hang in clusters from the side shoots.

stages.name: Turning
stages.note: The berries pale, then blush pink; the first ones deepen to red.

stages.name: Ripe
stages.note: Clusters of soft red raspberries, ready to slip off their white cores.

blueberry@1.label: Blueberry
blueberry@1.note: A twiggy shrub of many canes, small elliptic leaves, hanging clusters of white urn-shaped bells, berries turning pink, then blue under a silvery bloom.

layer.label: 3 · Shrubs
layer.note: the bushes: berries, woody herbs

stages.name: Seed
stages.note: A tiny seed from a berry, on acid peaty soil, barely covered, kept moist and cool.

stages.name: Germination
stages.note: After a month a root goes down, a tiny hook comes up.

stages.name: Seedling
stages.note: Two tiny round seed leaves and the first small leaves.

stages.name: Young bush
stages.note: A twiggy little bush, its new stems red.

stages.name: Bush
stages.note: Canes from the crown, grey-barked below, fine twigs above, small elliptic leaves.

stages.name: Flowering
stages.note: Clusters of small white bells hang from last year’s twigs, the bees at them.

stages.name: Fruit set
stages.note: The bells drop; little green berries, each with a five-pointed crown.

stages.name: Green berries
stages.note: Clusters of hard green berries swelling.

stages.name: Colouring
stages.note: Berry by berry they turn pink, then purple-blue.

stages.name: Ripe
stages.note: Blue berries under a pale silvery bloom, picked over weeks.

rosemary@1.label: Rosemary
rosemary@1.note: Upright woody stems crowded with dark needle leaves, pale blue flowers along them in late winter.

layer.label: 3 · Shrubs
layer.note: the bushes: berries, woody herbs

stages.name: Seed
stages.note: A small brown seed, slow and fickle — most rosemary is grown from cuttings.

stages.name: Germination
stages.note: The radicle goes down, the hook comes up.

stages.name: Seed leaves
stages.note: Two small round seed leaves.

stages.name: True leaves
stages.note: The first pair of true leaves, already smelling of the herb.

stages.name: Young plant
stages.note: An upright stem crowded with dark needle leaves, white beneath.

stages.name: Bushing
stages.note: Several stems, the lower ones going woody.

stages.name: Woody
stages.note: An evergreen shrub of upright woody stems, resinous to the touch.

stages.name: Buds
stages.note: Buds in the leaf axils along last year’s shoots.

stages.name: Flowering
stages.note: Pale blue flowers all along the stems in late winter and spring.

stages.name: Seeding
stages.note: Flowering over; cut back the tips to keep it dense.

sage@1.label: Sage
sage@1.note: A shrub of soft, pebbled, silver-grey leaves on woody stems; violet-blue flowers in whorls up tall spikes.

layer.label: 3 · Shrubs
layer.note: the bushes: berries, woody herbs

stages.name: Seed
stages.note: A round dark seed, a few millimetres down.

stages.name: Germination
stages.note: The radicle goes down, the hook comes up.

stages.name: Seed leaves
stages.note: Two small round seed leaves.

stages.name: True leaves
stages.note: The first pair of true leaves, already smelling of the herb.

stages.name: Young plant
stages.note: Soft grey-green leaves, pebbled and felted.

stages.name: Bushing
stages.note: A low bush; its oldest stems turning woody.

stages.name: Woody
stages.note: An evergreen shrub on woody stems, the leaves silver-grey.

stages.name: Buds
stages.note: Tall flower spikes rise above the leaves in its second spring.

stages.name: Flowering
stages.note: Violet-blue two-lipped flowers in whorls up the spikes.

stages.name: Seeding
stages.note: Cut back after flowering, it pushes new soft growth.

coffee@1.label: Coffee
coffee@1.note: One upright stem, level branches in pairs tier on tier, glossy dark leaves; white star flowers crowding the leaf axils along the branches, then cherries turning yellow and red.

layer.label: 3 · Shrubs
layer.note: the bushes: berries, woody herbs

stages.name: Bean
stages.note: A coffee bean still in its parchment, sown fresh and flat side down, a centimetre deep in the shade.

stages.name: Germination
stages.note: The root goes down; the stem rises like a match, the parchment still on its head (the soldier).

stages.name: Seed leaves
stages.note: The parchment drops: two round, wavy seed leaves open like a butterfly.

stages.name: Sapling
stages.note: One upright stem of glossy dark leaves in pairs; the first pairs of level branches.

stages.name: Young shrub
stages.note: Two metres of shrub, its level branches tier on tier, the lowest the longest.

stages.name: Flowering
stages.note: After the first rains, white star flowers crowd the leaf axils along the branches, scented like jasmine — for two days.

stages.name: Fruit set
stages.note: Little green cherries set in clusters where the flowers were.

stages.name: Green cherries
stages.note: Clusters of hard green cherries along the branches, filling for months.

stages.name: Turning
stages.note: Cherry by cherry they yellow, then blush red.

stages.name: Ripe
stages.note: Glossy red cherries crowding the branches, two beans in each: picked by hand, the ripe ones only.

lavender@1.label: Lavender
lavender@1.note: A grey-green mound of narrow leaves on a woody base; long bare stalks above it, each tipped with a spike of purple whorls.

layer.label: 3 · Shrubs
layer.note: the bushes: berries, woody herbs

stages.name: Seed
stages.note: A small, shiny dark-brown seed pressed onto the surface: slow and uneven to come up — most lavender is grown from cuttings.

stages.name: Germination
stages.note: The radicle goes down, the hook comes up.

stages.name: Seed leaves
stages.note: Two small round seed leaves.

stages.name: True leaves
stages.note: Narrow grey-green leaves in pairs, already smelling of lavender.

stages.name: Young plant
stages.note: Upright stems crowded with narrow leaves, branching from low down.

stages.name: Bushing
stages.note: A round mound of grey-green, the oldest stems turning woody.

stages.name: Woody
stages.note: An evergreen sub-shrub on a woody base, half a metre across.

stages.name: Buds
stages.note: Its second summer: long bare stalks rise above the leaves, tipped with spikes of grey-violet buds.

stages.name: Flowering
stages.note: The spikes open, whorl over whorl of small purple flowers, loud with bees.

stages.name: Harvest
stages.note: Cut the stalks as the first flowers open and hang them to dry; then trim the mound back to keep it from going leggy.

elder@1.label: Elder
elder@1.note: A big arching shrub of many stems and feathered leaves: flat cream umbels of elderflower at the shoot tips, turning over into heavy drooping umbels of black berries on red stalks.

layer.label: 3 · Shrubs
layer.note: the bushes: berries, woody herbs

stages.name: Seed
stages.note: A tiny wrinkled seed from an elderberry, left by a blackbird, barely covered.

stages.name: Germination
stages.note: A root goes down; two small seed leaves come up.

stages.name: Seedling
stages.note: Its first true leaves in opposite pairs, already feathered into leaflets.

stages.name: Young bush
stages.note: Fast: soft green stems a metre and more in a year, their pith white.

stages.name: Bush
stages.note: A big shrub of many stems, corky grey, arching out under feathered leaves, five metres high.

stages.name: Flowering
stages.note: In June, flat cream umbels a hand across at the tips of the new shoots, smelling of muscat: picked for elderflower.

stages.name: Fruit set
stages.note: The tiny petals fall; the umbels fill with green beads and begin to bow.

stages.name: Green berries
stages.note: The umbels heavy with hard green berries, turning over on their stalks.

stages.name: Colouring
stages.note: The stalks redden, the berries go red-purple, then black.

stages.name: Ripe
stages.note: Heavy drooping umbels of glossy black berries on red stalks: cooked, never raw, for juice, syrup and jam.

sea-buckthorn@1.label: Sea buckthorn
sea-buckthorn@1.note: A thorny silver shrub that fixes nitrogen in nodules on its roots; narrow silvery leaves, and orange berries packed all along last year’s twigs.

layer.label: 3 · Shrubs
layer.note: the bushes: berries, woody herbs

stages.name: Seed
stages.note: A small glossy brown seed from an orange berry, a centimetre down in sandy soil.

stages.name: Germination
stages.note: A root goes down, two narrow seed leaves come up; soon Frankia, a soil bacterium, finds the roots.

stages.name: Seedling
stages.note: Narrow silvery leaves; little orange-brown nodules swelling on the roots, fixing nitrogen from the air.

stages.name: Young bush
stages.note: Thorny stems, suckering, the leaves silver beneath.

stages.name: Bush
stages.note: A thorny silver shrub of three metres, many-stemmed, its twigs ending in thorns.

stages.name: Flowering
stages.note: In April, before the leaves: tiny greenish flowers crowded along last year’s twigs (on the female bush; the wind brings the pollen from a male).

stages.name: Fruit set
stages.note: The narrow silver leaves unfold; little green berries set, packed along the twigs.

stages.name: Green berries
stages.note: The twigs crammed with hard green berries.

stages.name: Colouring
stages.note: The berries turn yellow, then orange.

stages.name: Ripe
stages.note: Orange berries packed all along the twigs among the silver leaves: sour, oily, rich in vitamin C; the twigs are cut and frozen to shake them off.

redcurrant@1.label: Redcurrant
redcurrant@1.note: An open bush of upright stems from the crown, lobed leaves, and from spurs on the two- and three-year-old wood, strigs of small cups that ripen into hanging strings of translucent red currants.

layer.label: 3 · Shrubs
layer.note: the bushes: berries, woody herbs

stages.name: Seed
stages.note: A small pale seed from a berry, sown in autumn: it needs a winter’s cold before it wakes.

stages.name: Germination
stages.note: In spring a root goes down, a hooked shoot comes up.

stages.name: Seed leaves
stages.note: Two small oval seed leaves, then the first lobed one.

stages.name: Young bush
stages.note: A whip of a stem and its side shoots, lobed leaves all along.

stages.name: Bush
stages.note: An open bush of upright stems from the crown, a metre and more, grey-brown bark, spurs on the older wood.

stages.name: Flowering
stages.note: From the spurs hang strigs of small greenish-yellow cups, a dozen and more to a strig.

stages.name: Fruit set
stages.note: The flowers fade; little green berries along each strig, the last few at its tip falling.

stages.name: Green berries
stages.note: Strigs of hard green berries, swelling.

stages.name: Turning
stages.note: The berries clear and blush, the top of each strig first.

stages.name: Ripe
stages.note: Strigs of translucent red currants hanging under the leaves, the seeds showing through.

blackcurrant@1.label: Blackcurrant
blackcurrant@1.note: A bushy stool of many stems from the ground, big aromatic lobed leaves, short strigs of pinkish bells on last year’s shoots and then big glossy black currants.

layer.label: 3 · Shrubs
layer.note: the bushes: berries, woody herbs

stages.name: Seed
stages.note: A small dark seed from a berry, sown in autumn to be chilled through the winter.

stages.name: Germination
stages.note: In spring a root goes down, a hooked shoot comes up.

stages.name: Seed leaves
stages.note: Two small seed leaves; the first true leaf already smells of blackcurrant.

stages.name: Young bush
stages.note: A young bush, several shoots from low down, big lobed leaves.

stages.name: Bush
stages.note: A bushy stool of many stems straight from the ground, renewed from below year by year, the leaves aromatic.

stages.name: Flowering
stages.note: Short strigs of pinkish-purple bells hang from last year’s shoots.

stages.name: Fruit set
stages.note: Little green berries, five to ten to a strig.

stages.name: Green berries
stages.note: Glossy green berries swelling on the young wood.

stages.name: Turning
stages.note: Green to bronze and purple, the top berries first.

stages.name: Ripe
stages.note: Strigs of big glossy black currants, sharp and rich, along last year’s shoots.

gooseberry@1.label: Gooseberry
gooseberry@1.note: Arching branches a metre high with sharp spines at every node, small lobed leaves in tufts; single hairy, veined berries hanging under the branches, green turning dark red.

layer.label: 3 · Shrubs
layer.note: the bushes: berries, woody herbs

stages.name: Seed
stages.note: A small seed from a berry, sown in autumn for the winter to chill.

stages.name: Germination
stages.note: A root down, a hooked shoot up.

stages.name: Seed leaves
stages.note: Two small oval seed leaves; the first spines already at the first nodes.

stages.name: Young bush
stages.note: A few spiny shoots, small lobed leaves in tufts.

stages.name: Bush
stages.note: A low bush of arching spiny branches a metre high, sharp spines at every node.

stages.name: Flowering
stages.note: Small green, purple-flushed bells hang in ones and twos under the branches.

stages.name: Fruit set
stages.note: Each bell leaves a little hairy berry behind it, its withered flower at its tip.

stages.name: Green berries
stages.note: Big green veined berries hanging under the branches, hard and sour.

stages.name: Turning
stages.note: The berries soften and blush, the veins showing pale.

stages.name: Ripe
stages.note: Plump dark red gooseberries, hairy and veined, sweet now.

blackberry@1.label: Blackberry
blackberry@1.note: Long thorny canes arching over to root where they touch the soil: leafy the first summer, the second their side shoots flower white and pink and bear clusters of drupelet berries, green, red and black at once.

layer.label: 3 · Shrubs
layer.note: the bushes: berries, woody herbs

stages.name: Seed
stages.note: A small hard pitted seed from a drupelet, sown in autumn: two winters, sometimes, before it wakes.

stages.name: Germination
stages.note: A root goes down, a hooked shoot comes up.

stages.name: Seed leaves
stages.note: Two small oval seed leaves, then a first leaf of three toothed leaflets.

stages.name: First cane
stages.note: A first prickly cane, green flushed red, arching over.

stages.name: Canes
stages.note: Long arching primocanes, two metres and more, their tips bowing to the soil and rooting there; leaves of five leaflets.

stages.name: Flowering
stages.note: The canes’ second summer: side shoots along them with sprays of white-pink flowers; new green canes rise from the crown.

stages.name: Fruit set
stages.note: The petals fall; little green knots of drupelets.

stages.name: Green berries
stages.note: Clusters of hard green berries on the side shoots.

stages.name: Turning
stages.note: Berry by berry, red, unevenly: green, red and black on one spray.

stages.name: Ripe
stages.note: Glossy black blackberries among the red and the green, picked over weeks.

aronia@1.label: Aronia
aronia@1.note: An upright suckering shrub near two metres, glossy oval leaves going red in autumn, flat white corymbs at the shoot tips, then heavy clusters of black chokeberries.

layer.label: 3 · Shrubs
layer.note: the bushes: berries, woody herbs

stages.name: Seed
stages.note: A tiny brown seed from a black berry, sown in autumn to be chilled through the winter.

stages.name: Germination
stages.note: In spring a root goes down, a hooked shoot comes up.

stages.name: Seed leaves
stages.note: Two small oval seed leaves, then glossy pointed ones.

stages.name: Young bush
stages.note: A few upright shoots, glossy oval leaves.

stages.name: Bush
stages.note: An upright, suckering bush near two metres: many stems from the ground, glossy dark leaves.

stages.name: Flowering
stages.note: Flat corymbs of small white flowers with pink anthers at the tips of the shoots.

stages.name: Fruit set
stages.note: Little green berries, a dozen and more to a cluster.

stages.name: Green berries
stages.note: Clusters of green berries, the shoots bowing under them.

stages.name: Turning
stages.note: Red, then purple, then black, cluster by cluster.

stages.name: Ripe
stages.note: Heavy clusters of glossy black chokeberries, astringent and dark; the first leaves turning red.

haskap@1.label: Haskap
haskap@1.note: A rounded bush of peeling brown stems and soft oval leaves in pairs; pale yellow trumpets in pairs in the leaf axils in March, then long blue berries under a silver bloom — the year’s first fruit.

layer.label: 3 · Shrubs
layer.note: the bushes: berries, woody herbs

stages.name: Seed
stages.note: A tiny brown seed from a blue berry, sown in autumn.

stages.name: Germination
stages.note: Early in spring a root goes down, a hooked shoot comes up.

stages.name: Seed leaves
stages.note: Two small round seed leaves, then oval leaves in opposite pairs.

stages.name: Young bush
stages.note: A little bush of thin shoots, the leaves in pairs, the bark already peeling.

stages.name: Bush
stages.note: A rounded bush a metre and a half high, brown peeling bark, soft oval leaves in pairs.

stages.name: Flowering
stages.note: The first of all to flower, in March frosts: pale yellow trumpets in pairs in the leaf axils.

stages.name: Fruit set
stages.note: Each pair of flowers sets a single berry, the two grown into one.

stages.name: Green berries
stages.note: Long green berries hanging in the leaf axils.

stages.name: Turning
stages.note: Green to purple to blue, under a silver bloom.

stages.name: Ripe
stages.note: Long blue berries under their bloom — the first fruit of the year, before the strawberries.

rose@1.label: Japanese rose
rose@1.note: A dense thicket of bristling stems, wrinkled leaves of seven leaflets, big single magenta flowers at the shoot tips all summer, and big round scarlet hips crowned by their sepals.

layer.label: 3 · Shrubs
layer.note: the bushes: berries, woody herbs

stages.name: Seed
stages.note: A hard pale achene from inside a hip, sown in autumn: it wants a winter, often two, before it comes up.

stages.name: Germination
stages.note: A root goes down, a hooked shoot comes up.

stages.name: Seed leaves
stages.note: Two oval seed leaves, then the first leaf of three wrinkled leaflets.

stages.name: Young bush
stages.note: A bristly young shoot, its leaves of five and seven leaflets.

stages.name: Bush
stages.note: A dense thicket a metre and a half high, suckering out, every stem bristling with prickles.

stages.name: Flowering
stages.note: Big single flowers, magenta-pink and scented, golden stamens, at the ends of the shoots.

stages.name: Fruit set
stages.note: The petals drop; the hips start to swell under their crown of sepals — while new flowers still open.

stages.name: Green berries
stages.note: Fat round green hips, flattened, their sepals standing up.

stages.name: Turning
stages.note: The hips turn orange, then scarlet.

stages.name: Ripe
stages.note: Big round red hips like little tomatoes among the wrinkled leaves, a last flower or two.

tomato@1.label: Tomato
tomato@1.note: From a flat hairy seed to a staked cordon: ragged compound leaves, trusses of nodding yellow stars, tomatoes ripening truss by truss from green through orange to red.

layer.label: 4 · Herbaceous
layer.note: soft plants that die back or are grown each year: vegetables and herbs

stages.name: Seed
stages.note: A flat, hairy, beige seed three millimetres across, half a centimetre down in warm soil.

stages.name: Germination
