stages.note: The radicle goes down; the hypocotyl arches up through the soil, the seed coat still on the seed leaves.

stages.name: Seed leaves
stages.note: Two long narrow cotyledons open on a hairy purple-green stem.

stages.name: True leaves
stages.note: The first compound leaves, their leaflets ragged and lobed, smelling of tomato when touched.

stages.name: Staked
stages.note: Planted out and tied to a cane: a leaf at every node, the stem thickening, roots from the buried stem.

stages.name: Flowering
stages.note: The first truss of nodding yellow stars opens; more trusses follow every three leaves.

stages.name: Fruit set
stages.note: The petals wither; small green tomatoes swell on the first truss, the next truss in flower.

stages.name: Green fruit
stages.note: Trusses of hard green tomatoes, full-sized below, smaller above; the lowest leaves yellow.

stages.name: Breaker
stages.note: The first truss breaks colour from the blossom end: yellow, orange, blushing red.

stages.name: Ripe
stages.note: Red trusses from the bottom up, green ones still swelling at the top: picking time.

oxheart@1.label: Oxheart tomato
oxheart@1.note: A tall slender cordon, its wispy leaves hanging as if wilted; few, huge heart-shaped tomatoes to a truss, ribbed at the shoulders, ripening late to a pinkish red.

layer.label: 4 · Herbaceous
layer.note: soft plants that die back or are grown each year: vegetables and herbs

stages.name: Seed
stages.note: A flat, hairy, beige seed, half a centimetre down: oxhearts are sown a few weeks before other tomatoes.

stages.name: Germination
stages.note: The radicle goes down; the hypocotyl hooks up through the soil.

stages.name: Seed leaves
stages.note: Two long narrow cotyledons on a hairy stem.

stages.name: True leaves
stages.note: The first compound leaves — already thinner and droopier than a round tomato’s.

stages.name: Staked
stages.note: Tied to a tall cane, slender and fast: its wispy leaves hang and twist, as if wilting. They are fine.

stages.name: Flowering
stages.note: The first truss opens, its first flower often a big double one: that becomes the largest fruit.

stages.name: Fruit set
stages.note: Only three to five fruit set per truss; each swells fast, already heart-shaped.

stages.name: Green fruit
stages.note: Heavy green hearts, broad-shouldered and ribbed, pulling the trusses down.

stages.name: Breaker
stages.note: About sixty-five days from the flower, the first heart blushes from its point up, its shoulders green the longest.

stages.name: Ripe
stages.note: Pink-red hearts of three or four hundred grams, meaty with few seeds; the stem nearly two metres high.

eggplant@1.label: Eggplant
eggplant@1.note: A forked bush of big soft grey-green leaves with purple midribs, nodding violet stars, long glossy black-purple fruit under spiny green calyxes.

layer.label: 4 · Herbaceous
layer.note: soft plants that die back or are grown each year: vegetables and herbs

stages.name: Seed
stages.note: A flat, kidney-shaped tan seed, half a centimetre down: eggplants want the soil warm, 25 °C and more.

stages.name: Germination
stages.note: The radicle goes down; the hypocotyl hooks up into the light.

stages.name: Seed leaves
stages.note: Two oval cotyledons on a short stem.

stages.name: True leaves
stages.note: The first true leaves: soft, felted, grey-green, the midrib already purple.

stages.name: Bushing
stages.note: Planted out, the stem forks into a bush of big wavy leaves.

stages.name: Flowering
stages.note: Nodding violet stars in the leaf axils, a yellow cone of anthers at their heart.

stages.name: Fruit set
stages.note: The petals fall; under each spiny green calyx a little violet fruit swells.

stages.name: Swelling
stages.note: The fruit lengthen and darken, hanging under the leaves.

stages.name: Glossy
stages.note: Full-sized and deep purple, the skin taut and shining: the time to pick.

stages.name: Harvest
stages.note: Branch after branch of black-purple fruit, new flowers still opening above.

lettuce@1.label: Lettuce
lettuce@1.note: A butterhead: a rosette of broad wavy leaves, the inner ones standing up and cupping over each other into a pale, buttery head.

layer.label: 4 · Herbaceous
layer.note: soft plants that die back or are grown each year: vegetables and herbs

stages.name: Seed
stages.note: A slender grey seed four millimetres long, barely covered: lettuce wants light to sprout.

stages.name: Germination
stages.note: The radicle goes down, the hook comes up.

stages.name: Seed leaves
stages.note: Two small oval seed leaves.

stages.name: True leaves
stages.note: Soft, round, pale green true leaves.

stages.name: Rosette
stages.note: A flat rosette of broad wavy leaves.

stages.name: Heart forming
stages.note: The new leaves stay upright and start to cup round each other.

stages.name: Heading
stages.note: The inner leaves fold over the heart: a head is forming.

stages.name: Firming
stages.note: The head fills and firms, pale yellow-green inside.

stages.name: Full head
stages.note: A round, buttery head inside a ruff of spreading outer leaves.

stages.name: Harvest
stages.note: Cut it now — before it bolts.

pepper@1.label: Bell pepper
pepper@1.note: A little forking bush of glossy pointed leaves, a white flower nodding in every fork, blocky bells hanging green, then turning red.

layer.label: 4 · Herbaceous
layer.note: soft plants that die back or are grown each year: vegetables and herbs

stages.name: Seed
stages.note: A flat round pale seed, half a centimetre down in warm soil: peppers want 25 °C to sprout.

stages.name: Germination
stages.note: The radicle goes down, the hook comes up.

stages.name: Seed leaves
stages.note: Two long narrow seed leaves.

stages.name: True leaves
stages.note: Glossy, pointed, dark green true leaves.

stages.name: Forking
stages.note: The stem forks, and forks again, into a little bush.

stages.name: Flowering
stages.note: A single small white flower nods in every fork.

stages.name: Fruit set
stages.note: The petals fall; a little green bell swells behind each.

stages.name: Green peppers
stages.note: Blocky green bells, three or four lobes, hanging heavy.

stages.name: Colouring
stages.note: They darken, then turn: chocolate, then red.

stages.name: Ripe
stages.note: Glossy red peppers, thick-walled and sweet.

pineapple@1.label: Pineapple
pineapple@1.note: From a crown: a rosette of stiff spiny grey-green leaves; a red cone of violet flowers rises from its heart and fuses into one fruit, its eyes in spirals, yellowing from the base.

layer.label: 4 · Herbaceous
layer.note: soft plants that die back or are grown each year: vegetables and herbs

stages.name: Crown
stages.note: The leafy crown twisted off a ripe pineapple, dried a few days, set in the soil.

stages.name: Rooting
stages.note: Roots break from the base of the crown; its old leaves hold on.

stages.name: New leaves
stages.note: New leaves from the heart, longer than the crown’s.

stages.name: Rosette
stages.note: A rosette of stiff, channelled, grey-green leaves edged with small spines.

stages.name: Big rosette
stages.note: A metre across, forty leaves and more, the old crown leaves gone.

stages.name: Flowering
stages.note: A red cone rises from the heart; its violet flowers open a few each day, from the bottom up.

stages.name: Fruitlets
stages.note: Each flower’s fruit swells and fuses with its neighbours’; a little crown of leaves on top.

stages.name: Green fruit
stages.note: A green-grey pineapple, its eyes in spirals, growing on its stalk.

stages.name: Colouring
stages.note: It yellows from the base up, eye by eye.

stages.name: Ripe
stages.note: Golden, fragrant at its base: ripe. A slip already grows below it.

basil@1.label: Basil
basil@1.note: Glossy cupped leaves in pairs on a soft square stem, pinched into a bush; white whorled flower spikes; an annual.

layer.label: 4 · Herbaceous
layer.note: soft plants that die back or are grown each year: vegetables and herbs

stages.name: Seed
stages.note: A tiny black seed that turns jelly-coated when wet, barely covered: basil wants warmth and light.

stages.name: Germination
stages.note: The radicle goes down, the hook comes up.

stages.name: Seed leaves
stages.note: Two small round seed leaves.

stages.name: True leaves
stages.note: The first pair of true leaves, already smelling of the herb.

stages.name: Young plant
stages.note: Pairs of glossy cupped leaves up a soft square stem.

stages.name: Pinched
stages.note: The tip pinched out: two side shoots from every axil, a bushy plant.

stages.name: Bushy
stages.note: A bush of bright green, cupped, sweet-smelling leaves: harvest from the top.

stages.name: Buds
stages.note: Flower spikes form at the tips.

stages.name: Flowering
stages.note: White whorled spikes, loud with bees; the leaves now fewer and sharper.

stages.name: Seeding
stages.note: The spikes brown and set seed; an annual, it is done for the year.

parsley@1.label: Parsley
parsley@1.note: A rosette of flat, divided, toothed leaves through its first year; in its second, a stem of yellow-green umbels and ribbed seeds.

layer.label: 4 · Herbaceous
layer.note: soft plants that die back or are grown each year: vegetables and herbs

stages.name: Seed
stages.note: A ribbed grey-brown seed, slow: three or four weeks to come up.

stages.name: Germination
stages.note: The radicle goes down, the hook comes up.

stages.name: Seed leaves
stages.note: Two small round seed leaves.

stages.name: True leaves
stages.note: The first pair of true leaves, already smelling of the herb.

stages.name: Rosette
stages.note: A rosette of flat, deeply divided, toothed leaves on long stalks: cut from the outside.

stages.name: Full rosette
stages.note: A full dark-green rosette, cut and cut again all summer.

stages.name: Winter
stages.note: It sits through the winter, a few leaves green.

stages.name: Bolting
stages.note: Its second spring: a stem shoots up from the middle.

stages.name: Flowering
stages.note: Flat umbels of tiny yellow-green flowers.

stages.name: Seeding
stages.note: Ribbed seeds ripen and brown; the plant dies, having seeded.

chives@1.label: Chives
chives@1.note: A clump of little bulbs and hollow tubular leaves, cut and cut again; purple pompoms in its second spring.

layer.label: 4 · Herbaceous
layer.note: soft plants that die back or are grown each year: vegetables and herbs

stages.name: Seed
stages.note: A small black angular seed, a centimetre down.

stages.name: Germination
stages.note: The radicle goes down, the hook comes up.

stages.name: Seed leaves
stages.note: Two small round seed leaves.

stages.name: True leaves
stages.note: The first pair of true leaves, already smelling of the herb.

stages.name: Grass
stages.note: Thin hollow green leaves like fine grass.

stages.name: Tuft
stages.note: A tuft of tubular leaves from little bulbs.

stages.name: Clump
stages.note: A dense clump, cut down and growing back again and again.

stages.name: Buds
stages.note: Its second spring: buds in papery sheaths on firm stalks.

stages.name: Flowering
stages.note: Purple pompoms of little star flowers — edible too.

stages.name: Seeding
stages.note: The heads dry and drop black seeds; cut back, it grows fresh leaves.

mint@1.label: Mint
mint@1.note: Toothed wrinkled leaves on purplish square stems, runners rooting all round it, lilac flower spikes.

layer.label: 4 · Herbaceous
layer.note: soft plants that die back or are grown each year: vegetables and herbs

stages.name: Seed
stages.note: A dust-fine brown seed on the surface — or, as most do, a piece of runner from a friend.

stages.name: Germination
stages.note: The radicle goes down, the hook comes up.

stages.name: Seed leaves
stages.note: Two small round seed leaves.

stages.name: True leaves
stages.note: The first pair of true leaves, already smelling of the herb.

stages.name: Young plant
stages.note: Toothed, wrinkled leaves in pairs on a purplish square stem.

stages.name: Running
stages.note: Runners creep out over and under the soil, rooting as they go.

stages.name: Spreading
stages.note: A patch: new shoots come up wherever the runners root. Plant it in a pot or it takes the garden.

stages.name: Buds
stages.note: Slim flower spikes at the tips.

stages.name: Flowering
stages.note: Lilac whorled spikes humming with bees and butterflies.

stages.name: Seeding
stages.note: The spikes brown; the runners keep spreading underground.

lemon-balm@1.label: Lemon balm
lemon-balm@1.note: A clump of bright, crinkled, heart-shaped lemony leaves; small white flowers in the axils.

layer.label: 4 · Herbaceous
layer.note: soft plants that die back or are grown each year: vegetables and herbs

stages.name: Seed
stages.note: A small dark seed on the surface, kept moist.

stages.name: Germination
stages.note: The radicle goes down, the hook comes up.

stages.name: Seed leaves
stages.note: Two small round seed leaves.

stages.name: True leaves
stages.note: The first pair of true leaves, already smelling of the herb.

stages.name: Young plant
stages.note: Bright green, heart-shaped, toothed and crinkled leaves, smelling of lemon.

stages.name: Bushing
stages.note: A dense clump of upright branching stems.

stages.name: Clump
stages.note: A clump half a metre high and wide; it self-seeds freely.

stages.name: Buds
stages.note: Tiny buds in the leaf axils along the upper stems.

stages.name: Flowering
stages.note: Small white flowers in the axils: Melissa, the bees’ herb.

stages.name: Seeding
stages.note: It seeds everywhere unless cut back after flowering.

dill@1.label: Dill
dill@1.note: Thread-fine blue-green leaves, a single hollow stem, big umbels of yellow flowers, then flat seeds.

layer.label: 4 · Herbaceous
layer.note: soft plants that die back or are grown each year: vegetables and herbs

stages.name: Seed
stages.note: A flat oval ribbed seed, a centimetre down, straight where it is to grow.

stages.name: Germination
stages.note: The radicle goes down, the hook comes up.

stages.name: Seed leaves
stages.note: Two small round seed leaves.

stages.name: True leaves
stages.note: The first pair of true leaves, already smelling of the herb.

stages.name: Feathery
stages.note: Thread-fine blue-green leaves, a feathery plume.

stages.name: Stem
stages.note: A single hollow, ribbed stem shoots up, feathery leaves along it.

stages.name: Tall
stages.note: A metre of blue-green stem.

stages.name: Umbels
stages.note: Big flat umbels of tiny yellow flowers, like fireworks.

stages.name: Flowering
stages.note: Umbel after umbel open; the hoverflies come.

stages.name: Seeding
stages.note: Flat seeds ripen brown in the umbels: dill seed, for pickles.

coriander@1.label: Coriander
coriander@1.note: Broad lobed leaves first, feathery upper ones as it bolts; lacy white umbels, then round seeds.

layer.label: 4 · Herbaceous
layer.note: soft plants that die back or are grown each year: vegetables and herbs

stages.name: Seed
stages.note: A round, ridged, pale brown seed — it is two seeds in one husk.

stages.name: Germination
stages.note: The radicle goes down, the hook comes up.

stages.name: Seed leaves
stages.note: Two small round seed leaves.

stages.name: True leaves
stages.note: The first pair of true leaves, already smelling of the herb.

stages.name: Leafy
stages.note: Broad, rounded, lobed lower leaves: the coriander leaf (cilantro).

stages.name: Bolting
stages.note: A stem shoots up; its upper leaves are fine and feathery.

stages.name: Tall
stages.note: Branching stems, the leaf harvest over.

stages.name: Umbels
stages.note: Small umbels of white and pale pink flowers, the outer petals larger.

stages.name: Flowering
stages.note: Lacy white umbels everywhere.

stages.name: Seeding
stages.note: Round green seeds that ripen pale brown: coriander seed, the spice.

comfrey@1.label: Comfrey
comfrey@1.note: A clump of big bristly leaves over a deep black taproot; stems of curled cymes uncurling as their nodding purple bells open; cut and laid down as mulch, again and again.

layer.label: 4 · Herbaceous
layer.note: soft plants that die back or are grown each year: vegetables and herbs

stages.name: Root cutting
stages.note: A finger of comfrey root, black outside and white inside, laid five centimetres down in spring.

stages.name: Sprouting
stages.note: Buds break from its top; white roots from all along it.

stages.name: First leaves
stages.note: A few bristly, pointed leaves, rough to touch.

stages.name: Rosette
stages.note: Big lance leaves on winged stalks, spreading from the crown; the root turning black and going down.

stages.name: Clump
stages.note: Its second spring: a dense clump of leaves half a metre long; the taproot a metre down.

stages.name: Flowering stems
stages.note: Winged, bristly stems rise a metre from the clump, branching at the top.

stages.name: Buds
stages.note: At every tip a curled cyme like a scorpion’s tail, packed with buds.

stages.name: Flowering
stages.note: The cymes uncurl as their bells open one by one, nodding, a bumblebee at each.

stages.name: Full bloom
stages.note: Bells all along the uncurled cymes; the lowest leaves yellowing.

stages.name: Chop and drop
stages.note: Cut to a hand high and laid round it as mulch, feeding the soil; new leaves are up within days.

chard@1.label: Swiss chard
chard@1.note: A rosette of big glossy, blistered leaves on thick stalks — red, yellow, orange, pink or white by the seed — picked from the outside all summer.

layer.label: 4 · Herbaceous
layer.note: soft plants that die back or are grown each year: vegetables and herbs

stages.name: Seed
stages.note: A corky, knobbly seed cluster (several seeds in one), two centimetres down.

stages.name: Germination
stages.note: One cluster, two or three seedlings: the radicles go down, the hooks come up.

stages.name: Seed leaves
stages.note: Two long narrow seed leaves on a stem already red, yellow or white.

stages.name: True leaves
stages.note: The first true leaves, glossy, on coloured stalks.

stages.name: Rosette
stages.note: A rosette of glossy, blistered leaves on broad stalks.

stages.name: Baby leaf
stages.note: Leaves a hand long: picked young for salads.

stages.name: First picking
stages.note: The outer leaves full-sized: twist them off at the base.

stages.name: Cut and come again
stages.note: Picked from the outside, new leaves keep coming from the middle.

stages.name: Full
stages.note: Big crinkled leaves, half a metre tall on thick bright stalks.

stages.name: Harvest
stages.note: Picked all summer and into the autumn; it stands the first frosts.

kale@1.label: Kale
kale@1.note: An upright stem crowned with blue-green leaves, curled and frilled or long and blistered (Lacinato); picked from the bottom up, the stem bare and scarred like a little palm.

layer.label: 4 · Herbaceous
layer.note: soft plants that die back or are grown each year: vegetables and herbs

stages.name: Seed
stages.note: A round dark-brown seed two millimetres across, a centimetre down.

stages.name: Germination
stages.note: The radicle goes down, the hook comes up.

stages.name: Seed leaves
stages.note: Two heart-shaped seed leaves, notched at the tip, on a purplish stem.

stages.name: True leaves
stages.note: The first true leaves, already blue-green and waxy.

stages.name: Young plant
stages.note: A rosette on a short, stout stem.

stages.name: Leafy
stages.note: Big leaves on long stalks, new ones from the top as the stem lengthens.

stages.name: First picking
stages.note: The lowest leaves snapped off down at the stem, leaving scars.

stages.name: Picking
stages.note: Picked from the bottom up week by week; the stem rises bare and scarred.

stages.name: Winter
stages.note: Frost sweetens it: a crown of leaves on a scarred stem, like a little palm.

stages.name: Harvest
stages.note: Still picking from the crown through the winter; in spring it will flower.

rhubarb@1.label: Rhubarb
rhubarb@1.note: From a knobbly crown, red buds and huge crinkled leaves on thick red stalks — pulled from the outside in its second spring — then a hollow stem two metres high with a cream plume.

layer.label: 4 · Herbaceous
layer.note: soft plants that die back or are grown each year: vegetables and herbs

stages.name: Crown
stages.note: A division of an old crown — a fat red bud or two on a piece of knobbly rootstock — set level with the soil in late winter.

stages.name: Bud break
stages.note: Red knobbly buds push through the soil, the crumpled leaves packed tight inside them.

stages.name: Unfurling
stages.note: The first leaves unfurl, crinkled and bronze-green, on short red stalks.

stages.name: First summer
stages.note: A clump of big leaves; none pulled in the first year, so the crown can build.

stages.name: Second spring
stages.note: Back from the winter with more buds, broader leaves and thicker stalks.

stages.name: Full clump
stages.note: Leaves half a metre across on stalks thick as a thumb, the clump a metre and more wide.

stages.name: First pull
stages.note: The first stalks pulled — held low and twisted off the crown, never cut — a few only.

stages.name: Pulling
stages.note: Pulled from the outside week by week, the leaves cut off onto the compost (they are poisonous); never more than a third, and no more after midsummer.

stages.name: Flower spike
stages.note: A thick hollow stem shoots up two metres from the crown, papery sheaths at its nodes, a great plume of tiny cream flowers.

stages.name: Seed
stages.note: The plume turns rusty red with winged seeds; the old leaves yellow at their edges. (Cut the spike early and the crown keeps its strength.)

sorrel@1.label: Sorrel
sorrel@1.note: A clump of long-stalked, arrow-shaped, lemon-sour leaves, picked from the outside; then slender stems of tiny reddish flowers turning rust-red with seed.

layer.label: 4 · Herbaceous
layer.note: soft plants that die back or are grown each year: vegetables and herbs

stages.name: Seed
stages.note: A small, glossy, three-sided brown seed, barely covered.

stages.name: Germination
stages.note: The radicle goes down, the hook comes up.

stages.name: Seed leaves
stages.note: Two narrow seed leaves.

stages.name: True leaves
stages.note: The first true leaves, already arrow-shaped and sharp with oxalic acid.

stages.name: Rosette
stages.note: A rosette of long-stalked arrow-shaped leaves, the stalks red at the base.

stages.name: Clump
stages.note: A dense clump a hand and a half high; a reddish taproot below. It comes back every spring.

stages.name: First picking
stages.note: Its second spring, the first green of the year: the young leaves picked for soup and sauce, lemony and sour.

stages.name: Cut and come again
stages.note: Picked from the outside, new leaves keep coming from the middle.

stages.name: Flowering
stages.note: Slender stems rise knee-high with whorls of tiny reddish flowers up their branches.

stages.name: Seeding
stages.note: The spikes turn rust-red with winged seeds; cut them off and the leaves come again.

nettle@1.label: Stinging nettle
nettle@1.note: From a tiny seed to a patch on creeping yellow rhizomes: square stems a metre high, toothed heart leaves in pairs, green flower tassels hanging from the upper axils.

layer.label: 4 · Herbaceous
layer.note: soft plants that die back or are grown each year: vegetables and herbs

stages.name: Seed
stages.note: A tiny flat oval seed, one of the thousands a female plant shed last autumn, on bare rich soil.

stages.name: Germination
stages.note: The radicle goes down, the hook comes up.

stages.name: Seed leaves
stages.note: Two small round seed leaves.

stages.name: True leaves
stages.note: The first pair of toothed leaves, already bristling with stinging hairs.

stages.name: Young plant
stages.note: A square stem with heart-shaped, toothed leaves in pairs, each pair turned a quarter from the last.

stages.name: Spreading
stages.note: Yellow rhizomes creep out under the soil and send up new stems: a patch.

stages.name: Picking tops
stages.note: Its second spring: the top four leaves of every stem picked, with gloves, for soup, tea and pesto; the patch grows back thicker.

stages.name: Flowering
stages.note: Stems a metre high and more; green tassels of tiny flowers hang in pairs from the upper leaf axils, male and female on separate plants.

stages.name: Seeding
stages.note: The female tassels heavy and drooping with seed; the caterpillars of peacock and small tortoiseshell butterflies on the leaves.

stages.name: Seed harvest
stages.note: Seed for picking, the tassels brown-green; cut down, the stems are the best compost activator and a liquid feed.

artichoke@1.label: Globe artichoke
artichoke@1.note: A fountain of deeply cut silver-grey leaves; ribbed stems carry the scaly buds that are eaten, or left to open into violet thistles.

layer.label: 4 · Herbaceous
layer.note: soft plants that die back or are grown each year: vegetables and herbs

stages.name: Offset
stages.note: A rooted offset sliced from the side of an old plant with a heel of root, planted in spring.

stages.name: Rooting
stages.note: New white roots below; from its heart a first new leaf.

stages.name: New leaves
stages.note: Grey-green leaves, deeply cut, rising in a fountain.

stages.name: Fountain
stages.note: A fountain of silver leaves near a metre long, arching over; mulched against the winter.

stages.name: Big clump
stages.note: Its second spring: a clump of silver leaves a metre and a half across.

stages.name: Stems
stages.note: Thick, ribbed grey stems rise from the heart, a bud at every tip.

stages.name: Buds
stages.note: The king bud at the top of each stem, smaller ones on the side shoots, scale over scale.

stages.name: Harvest
stages.note: Cut while tight and fist-sized, the scales still closed: their fleshy bases and the heart are eaten. A few are left.

stages.name: Opening
stages.note: A bud left on loosens its scales; a violet tuft shows at the top.

stages.name: Thistle
stages.note: A violet thistle a hand across, loud with bumblebees; cut the stems down after and new shoots come from the base.

asparagus@1.label: Asparagus
asparagus@1.note: From a spidery crown, spears every spring — left for two years, then cut for six weeks — and feathery fern a metre and a half high, red berries on the female plants.

layer.label: 4 · Herbaceous
layer.note: soft plants that die back or are grown each year: vegetables and herbs

stages.name: Crown
stages.note: A one-year crown like a big pale spider, its fleshy roots spread over a ridge in a trench, twenty centimetres down, in spring.

stages.name: First spears
stages.note: Thin spears push up through the soil; none are cut for two years, so the crown can build.

stages.name: First fern
stages.note: The spears open into airy fern half a metre high: not leaves but needle-fine little stems.

stages.name: Golden fern
stages.note: In the autumn the fern turns gold, feeding the crown below; then it is cut down.

stages.name: Second spring
stages.note: More spears and thicker, still left to grow.

stages.name: Second summer
stages.note: Fern a metre high, a little thicket of feathers.

stages.name: Spears
stages.note: Its third spring: fat spears, cut a little under the soil when twenty centimetres tall, every day or two.

stages.name: Cutting
stages.note: Six weeks of cutting; then the spears are left to grow, to feed the crown for next year.

stages.name: Fern and flowers
stages.note: Fern a metre and a half high; tiny green-white bells hang along it.

stages.name: Berries
stages.note: On the female plants, red berries among the feathers; the fern goes gold in the autumn.

hemp@1.label: Hemp
hemp@1.note: One slender stalk two and a half metres high in a summer, leaves of five to nine toothed leaflets spread like hands; seed in clusters of bracts at the top, the stalk retted for its fibre.

layer.label: 4 · Herbaceous
layer.note: soft plants that die back or are grown each year: vegetables and herbs

stages.name: Seed
stages.note: A small smooth grey-brown seed, marbled, two centimetres down in warm spring soil — sown thick, so the stalks grow tall and slender.

stages.name: Germination
stages.note: The radicle goes down, the hook comes up.

stages.name: Seed leaves
stages.note: Two small oval seed leaves.

stages.name: First pairs
stages.note: The first true leaves in pairs: a single toothed leaflet, then three, then five.

stages.name: Vegetative
stages.note: Growing fast, leaves of seven and nine leaflets spread like hands, in pairs a quarter-turn apart.

stages.name: Stretch
stages.note: Shooting up two metres and more, the leaves now one at a node, spiralling up the stalk.

stages.name: Flowering
stages.note: At the top and the short side shoots, clusters of small bracts with white pistils; the pollen drifts in the wind.

stages.name: Seed set
stages.note: Seeds swell in the bracts; the lowest leaves yellow.

stages.name: Ripening
stages.note: The seed heads turn brown-grey, the leaves fall from the bottom up.

stages.name: Harvest
stages.note: Seed threshed from the heads; the bare stalks cut and laid in the field to ret for their fibre.

lentil@1.label: Lentil
lentil@1.note: A low, fine, bushy annual of feathery leaves ending in little tendrils; tiny white-lilac flowers, small flat pods of one or two lentils, the whole plant drying to straw.

layer.label: 4 · Herbaceous
layer.note: soft plants that die back or are grown each year: vegetables and herbs

stages.name: Seed
stages.note: A small flat lens of a seed, green-brown, two or three centimetres down in early spring — it does not mind the cold.

stages.name: Germination
stages.note: The root goes down; the seed itself stays below, and a hooked shoot pushes up from it.

stages.name: First leaves
stages.note: Above two scale leaves, the first leaf: a pair of small oval leaflets and a bristle.

stages.name: Seedling
stages.note: Leaves of more leaflet pairs, side stems from the base.

stages.name: Branching
stages.note: A low, fine, bushy plant, feathery pinnate leaves ending in little tendrils that catch on its neighbours.

stages.name: Flowering
stages.note: Tiny white flowers veined with lilac, one or two on a short stalk from the upper axils.

stages.name: Pods set
stages.note: Behind the flowers, small flat pods.

stages.name: Green pods
stages.note: Pods full, one or two lentils in each; on the roots, the pink nodules have been fixing nitrogen all along.

stages.name: Drying
stages.note: Leaves yellowing from the bottom up, the pods turning tan.

stages.name: Harvest
stages.note: The whole plant dry and straw-coloured, the lentils rattling in their pods: pulled or cut, and threshed.

edamame@1.label: Edamame
edamame@1.note: An upright, hairy bush of leaves of three; small purple flowers in the axils, then clusters of fuzzy green pods all along the stem, picked plump as edamame — or left to yellow for dry soybeans.

layer.label: 4 · Herbaceous
layer.note: soft plants that die back or are grown each year: vegetables and herbs

stages.name: Seed
stages.note: A round soybean, green for edamame, three centimetres down in warm soil after the last frost.

stages.name: Germination
stages.note: The root goes down; a hooked stem pulls the bean up and out of the soil.

stages.name: Seed leaves
stages.note: The bean splits into two fat yellow-green seed leaves, held up in the light.

stages.name: First leaves
stages.note: A pair of simple oval leaves, opposite, above the seed leaves.

stages.name: Trifoliates
stages.note: Leaves of three on long stalks, one at a node, everything soft with tawny hairs; side stems from the lower nodes.

stages.name: Flowering
stages.note: Small purple (or white) flowers tucked in clusters in the leaf axils, all the way up.

stages.name: Pods set
stages.note: Flat little pods, two to four at a node.

stages.name: Filling
stages.note: The pods fattening, fuzzy and green, two or three beans showing in each.

stages.name: Picking
stages.note: Edamame: the pods plump and bright green — the whole plant pulled, or picked over, and the pods boiled in salt water.

stages.name: Dry beans
stages.note: Left on, the leaves yellow and fall, the pods turn tan and hard: soybeans for drying.

chickpea@1.label: Chickpea
chickpea@1.note: A grey-green, glandular-hairy bush of small toothed leaflets; white or pink flowers one to a stalk, then puffed-up pods with a chickpea or two, drying golden-tan.

layer.label: 4 · Herbaceous
layer.note: soft plants that die back or are grown each year: vegetables and herbs

stages.name: Seed
stages.note: A beige, wrinkled seed like a ram’s head (the dark desi ones smaller and angular), five centimetres down in warm spring soil.

stages.name: Germination
stages.note: The root goes down deep; the seed stays below, and a hooked shoot pushes up from it.

stages.name: First leaves
stages.note: Above two scale leaves, the first small pinnate leaves, grey-green and hairy.

stages.name: Seedling
stages.note: Several stems from the base, every part covered in fine glandular hairs, sour to the tongue.

stages.name: Branching
stages.note: A bushy upright plant half a metre high, leaves of small toothed leaflets, no tendrils.

stages.name: Flowering
stages.note: Small white or pink-purple flowers, one on each long stalk from the axils.

stages.name: Pods set
stages.note: Short, puffed-up pods like little balloons behind the flowers.

stages.name: Filling
stages.note: Pods full, hairy and pale green, a chickpea or two rattling inside each; picked green, they are eaten fresh.

stages.name: Drying
stages.note: The leaves yellow, the pods turn golden-tan.

stages.name: Harvest
stages.note: The plant dry and golden, the pods papery: pulled and threshed.

oats@1.label: Oats
oats@1.note: A tuft of tillers, long blades, stems a metre high with their nodes, and open nodding panicles of dangling spikelets, green and then golden over golden straw.

layer.label: 4 · Herbaceous
layer.note: soft plants that die back or are grown each year: vegetables and herbs

stages.name: Seed
stages.note: A slim, pale, hulled oat grain, three centimetres down in early spring.

stages.name: Germination
stages.note: Three seminal roots go down; the coleoptile, a pale sheath, pushes up to the light.

stages.name: First leaf
stages.note: The first blade unrolls out of the coleoptile, then the next out of the first.

stages.name: Tillering
stages.note: Side shoots from the crown at the soil: a tuft of blades, crown roots below.

stages.name: Stem extension
stages.note: The stems shoot up, a node at a time, each wrapped in its leaf’s sheath.

stages.name: Booting
stages.note: The panicle swells inside the sheath of the flag leaf, the last and broadest.

stages.name: Heading
stages.note: The panicle breaks out and opens: whorls of fine branches, the spikelets dangling from their tips, flowering within.

stages.name: Grain fill
stages.note: The grain milky, then doughy; the panicles heavier, nodding, still green.

stages.name: Turning
stages.note: Yellowing from the bottom up, the panicles golden-green.

stages.name: Harvest
stages.note: Golden straw, the spikelets papery and pale, the grain hard: cut and threshed.

strawberry@1.label: Strawberry
strawberry@1.note: From an achene on the soil to a rosette in fruit with a runner: trifoliate toothed leaves, white flowers, berries ripening from the tip.

layer.label: 5 · Ground cover
layer.note: low and spreading over the soil, keeping it covered

stages.name: Seed
stages.note: An achene a millimetre long, sown on the soil, barely covered: strawberry seeds want light to sprout.

stages.name: Germination
stages.note: The radicle breaks out and turns down; the hypocotyl, bent in a hook, pushes up into the light.

stages.name: Seed leaves
stages.note: Two round cotyledons open on a stem a centimetre high; the root has its first laterals.

stages.name: True leaves
stages.note: The first trifoliate leaves, toothed, from between the seed leaves: the crown has begun.

stages.name: Rosette
stages.note: A crown of leaves on long stalks, the seed leaves gone, fibrous roots spreading from the crown.

stages.name: Flowering
stages.note: Trusses of white five-petalled flowers rise between the leaves, bees welcome.

stages.name: Fruit set
stages.note: The petals fall; behind each flower the receptacle swells into a small green berry, its seeds standing out.

stages.name: Green berries
stages.note: The berries fill out, still hard and green, their stalks bowing toward the soil; a runner sets out.

stages.name: Turning
stages.note: The first berries pale to white and blush red from the tip up; a daughter plant roots at the runner’s end.

stages.name: Ripe
stages.note: Berry after berry red and glossy, hanging on the straw: picking time.

pumpkin@1.label: Pumpkin
pumpkin@1.note: A vine running along the ground, rooting at its nodes, huge lobed leaves standing up, big yellow trumpets, ribbed pumpkins lying on the soil turning deep orange.

layer.label: 5 · Ground cover
layer.note: low and spreading over the soil, keeping it covered

stages.name: Seed
stages.note: A big flat cream seed, two and a half centimetres down in warm soil.

stages.name: Germination
stages.note: The radicle goes down; the hook pulls the seed leaves out of the coat.

stages.name: Seed leaves
stages.note: Two big oval seed leaves.

stages.name: True leaves
stages.note: The first rough, lobed true leaves.

stages.name: Running
stages.note: The vine runs along the ground, a huge leaf standing up at every node, rooting as it goes.

stages.name: Flowering
stages.note: Big yellow trumpets open at dawn: male ones on long stalks, female ones on a little round ovary.

stages.name: Fruit set
stages.note: The bees have been: the ovaries swell into small green pumpkins lying on the soil.

stages.name: Green pumpkins
stages.note: Ribbed pumpkins growing fast, still green.

stages.name: Colouring
stages.note: They turn deep orange from the top, the stalk hardening.

stages.name: Ripe
stages.note: Deep orange Hokkaidos, the stalks corky and dry, the leaves going over: harvest.

moss@1.label: Haircap moss
moss@1.note: From a spore: a green thread over the soil, buds, star-like leafy shoots crowding into a cushion and a carpet; red-brown stalks with hairy-capped capsules that ripen and shed their spores.

layer.label: 5 · Ground cover
layer.note: low and spreading over the soil, keeping it covered

stages.name: Spore
stages.note: A moss spore, a hundredth of a millimetre, landed on damp shaded soil.

stages.name: Protonema
stages.note: A green thread creeps over the soil, branching: the protonema.

stages.name: Buds
stages.note: Tiny buds swell on the threads, each the start of a shoot; brown rhizoids anchor them.

stages.name: Leafy shoots
stages.note: Upright shoots, narrow leaves in a spiral, star-like from above.

stages.name: Cushion
stages.note: The shoots crowd together into a soft dark-green cushion.

stages.name: Carpet
stages.note: The cushion spreads into a carpet, holding the rain like a sponge.

stages.name: Sporophytes
stages.note: From the female shoots, red-brown stalks rise, each with a capsule under a golden hairy cap.

stages.name: Capsules
stages.note: The capsules swell, four-angled, their caps still on.

stages.name: Ripe capsules
stages.note: The caps fall, the capsules brown and tilt.

stages.name: Spores
stages.note: The lids pop off; spores drift out on dry days. The carpet keeps on growing.

wild-garlic@1.label: Wild garlic
wild-garlic@1.note: A woodland bulb from a seed that needs a winter’s cold: years later, two or three broad garlicky leaves, a ball of white stars, then gone till next spring.

layer.label: 5 · Ground cover
layer.note: low and spreading over the soil, keeping it covered

stages.name: Seed
stages.note: A small black seed dropped in the leaf litter of a damp beech wood in early summer.

stages.name: Winter cold
stages.note: It needs a winter’s cold before it will wake.

stages.name: Germination
stages.note: In early spring a root, and a single thread-like leaf.

stages.name: First bulb
stages.note: A tiny bulb forms; the leaf yellows and is gone by summer.

stages.name: Young plant
stages.note: Its second spring: one narrow leaf on a stalk, the bulb a little bigger.

stages.name: Spring leaves
stages.note: In its third or fourth spring, two or three broad bright-green leaves: Bärlauch, smelling strongly of garlic.

stages.name: Bud
stages.note: A bud rises on a three-sided stalk, wrapped in a papery spathe.

stages.name: Flowering
stages.note: The spathe splits: a loose ball of white six-pointed stars. The wood floor goes white.

stages.name: Seeds
stages.note: Green three-lobed capsules swell where the stars were; the leaves begin to yellow.

stages.name: Dieback
stages.note: The leaves die back to the bulb; the seeds drop; above ground, nothing until next March.

thyme@1.label: Thyme
thyme@1.note: A little woody evergreen shrub of wiry stems and tiny leaves, clouds of pink flowers at the tips.

layer.label: 5 · Ground cover
layer.note: low and spreading over the soil, keeping it covered

stages.name: Seed
stages.note: A seed like dust, sown on the surface: thyme wants light.

stages.name: Germination
stages.note: The radicle goes down, the hook comes up.

stages.name: Seed leaves
stages.note: Two small round seed leaves.

stages.name: True leaves
stages.note: The first pair of true leaves, already smelling of the herb.

stages.name: Young plant
stages.note: Wiry stems with tiny pointed leaves in pairs.

stages.name: Bushing
stages.note: A dense mound of wiry branches.

stages.name: Woody
stages.note: A little evergreen shrub, its stems woody and twisted.

stages.name: Buds
stages.note: Tiny buds crowd the shoot tips.

stages.name: Flowering
stages.note: Clouds of tiny pink flowers, alive with bees.

stages.name: Seeding
stages.note: Trimmed after flowering, it stays compact for years.

oregano@1.label: Oregano
oregano@1.note: A low mat of small round leaves sending up branching stems topped with clusters of pink-purple flowers.

layer.label: 5 · Ground cover
layer.note: low and spreading over the soil, keeping it covered

stages.name: Seed
stages.note: A seed like dust, sown on the surface.

stages.name: Germination
stages.note: The radicle goes down, the hook comes up.

stages.name: Seed leaves
stages.note: Two small round seed leaves.

stages.name: True leaves
stages.note: The first pair of true leaves, already smelling of the herb.

stages.name: Young plant
stages.note: A low mat of small round downy leaves.

stages.name: Spreading
stages.note: Creeping stems spread the mat wide.

stages.name: Upright
stages.note: Upright stems rise from the mat.

stages.name: Buds
stages.note: The stems branch at their tops into tight bud clusters.

stages.name: Flowering
stages.note: Flat clusters of tiny pink-purple flowers with purple bracts: the bees’ favourite.

stages.name: Seeding
stages.note: Cut the stems in flower and dry them: that is when it tastes strongest.

clover@1.label: White clover
clover@1.note: Stolons creeping over the soil and rooting at every node; leaves of three with a pale chevron, round white flower heads, pink nodules on the roots fixing nitrogen.

layer.label: 5 · Ground cover
layer.note: low and spreading over the soil, keeping it covered

stages.name: Seed
stages.note: A tiny yellow, heart-shaped seed, pressed onto the soil’s surface.

stages.name: Germination
stages.note: The radicle goes down, the hook comes up.

stages.name: Seed leaves
stages.note: Two small round seed leaves on a short stem.

stages.name: First leaf
stages.note: A single round first leaf on its stalk, then the first leaf of three.

stages.name: Creeping
stages.note: Stolons run out over the soil, rooting at every node, a leaf of three at each.

stages.name: Mat
stages.note: A mat of leaves on long stalks, every leaflet with a pale chevron; pink nodules on the roots fixing nitrogen.

stages.name: Flowering
stages.note: Round white flower heads on stalks taller than the leaves, the bees at them all day.

stages.name: Full flower
stages.note: Heads everywhere over the mat, the oldest florets folding down.

stages.name: Setting seed
stages.note: The florets brown and hang, tiny pods inside them.

stages.name: Seed
stages.note: Brown, dry heads full of seed; the mat creeps on, feeding the soil with its nitrogen.

nasturtium@1.label: Nasturtium
nasturtium@1.note: Trailing stems over the soil, round shield leaves with the stalk at the middle, spurred flowers orange, red or yellow, and wrinkled green seeds in threes.

layer.label: 5 · Ground cover
layer.note: low and spreading over the soil, keeping it covered

stages.name: Seed
stages.note: A big, wrinkled, ribbed seed like a dried chickpea, two centimetres down after the last frost.

stages.name: Germination
stages.note: The root goes down and the shoot comes up alone: the seed leaves stay below, in the seed.

stages.name: First leaves
stages.note: Round shield leaves on long stalks, the stalk joined at the middle; water beads and rolls off them.

stages.name: Leafy
stages.note: A little mound of round, pale-veined leaves.

stages.name: Trailing
stages.note: Stems sprawl out over the soil, a round leaf at every node.

stages.name: Spreading
stages.note: A mat of shield leaves a metre and more across, covering the soil under the fruit trees.

stages.name: Buds
stages.note: Spurred buds on long stalks from the leaf axils.

stages.name: Flowering
stages.note: Orange, red or yellow flowers, each with its long nectar spur; leaves and flowers both peppery, eaten in salad.

stages.name: Seeds set
stages.note: Behind each faded flower, three green wrinkled seeds joined in a triangle — pickled as poor man’s capers.

stages.name: Ripe seeds
stages.note: The seeds turn pale and drop, to come up again next year; it flowers on until the first frost blackens it.

woodruff@1.label: Sweet woodruff
woodruff@1.note: A low carpet for the deep shade: slender stems of starry leaf whorls, tiny white four-pointed flowers in May, then bristly burs; it smells of new hay as it dries.

layer.label: 5 · Ground cover
layer.note: low and spreading over the soil, keeping it covered

stages.name: Division
stages.note: A clump of thin pale rhizomes with a few shoots, planted in the shade under trees in autumn.

stages.name: Rooting
stages.note: New roots run through the leaf litter.

stages.name: First shoots
stages.note: In early spring, slender square stems push up, their leaves folded in tight stars.

stages.name: Whorls
stages.note: Stems a hand high, a whorl of six to nine narrow glossy leaves at every node, like little ruffs.

stages.name: Creeping
stages.note: Thin rhizomes creep out under the leaf litter and send up new stems.

stages.name: Carpet
stages.note: A year on: a bright green carpet in the deep shade, keeping the soil covered where little else grows.

stages.name: Buds
stages.note: Spring: buds at the stem tips. Now, before it flowers, it is picked and wilted for the Maibowle — the scent of coumarin, of new hay, comes as it dries.

stages.name: Flowering
stages.note: Loose sprays of tiny white four-pointed stars above the whorls.

stages.name: Burs
stages.note: Little round fruits covered in hooked bristles, that catch in fur and socks and are carried off.

stages.name: Summer carpet
stages.note: The burs ripen dark; the carpet stays green until the autumn.

radish@1.label: Radish
radish@1.note: Four weeks from seed: heart-shaped seed leaves, rough lobed leaves, the stem below them swelling into a red ball half out of the soil.

layer.label: 6 · Roots
layer.note: grown for what they swell below the soil: roots, tubers, bulbs

stages.name: Seed
stages.note: A round brown seed three millimetres across, a centimetre down.

stages.name: Germination
stages.note: Within two days the radicle is out and the hook breaks the soil.

stages.name: Seed leaves
stages.note: Two heart-shaped seed leaves, notched at their tips.

stages.name: True leaves
stages.note: The first rough, lobed true leaves.

stages.name: Rosette
stages.note: A small rosette; below, the stem between root and leaves begins to thicken.

stages.name: Swelling
stages.note: The hypocotyl turns red and swells at the soil’s surface.

stages.name: Rounding
stages.note: A red ball forming, its white tail root going down.

stages.name: Filling
stages.note: The ball fills out, its red shoulders pushing up out of the soil.

stages.name: Full
stages.note: Round and firm, two and a half centimetres across.

stages.name: Harvest
stages.note: Pull it now, crisp and hot — a week more and it goes woolly.

carrot@1.label: Carrot
carrot@1.note: Grass-like seed leaves, then a fountain of ferny leaves over a taproot thickening down its length into a long orange cone.

layer.label: 6 · Roots
layer.note: grown for what they swell below the soil: roots, tubers, bulbs

stages.name: Seed
stages.note: A tiny ridged, bristly seed, a centimetre down; carrots are slow to come up.

stages.name: Germination
stages.note: The radicle goes down long before anything shows above.

stages.name: Seed leaves
stages.note: Two long, grass-like seed leaves.

stages.name: True leaves
stages.note: The first finely divided, ferny true leaf.

stages.name: Ferny tops
stages.note: A fountain of ferny leaves; below, the taproot starts to thicken.

stages.name: Thickening
stages.note: The taproot fills out at the top and turns orange.

stages.name: Lengthening
stages.note: It thickens down its length, fine roots in rows along it.

stages.name: Colouring
stages.note: Deep orange through, its shoulders at the soil’s surface.

stages.name: Filling out
stages.note: Full, blunt-ended, sweet.

stages.name: Harvest
stages.note: Lift it now: twenty centimetres of carrot under the ferny top.

garlic@1.label: Garlic
garlic@1.note: A clove planted in autumn: roots from its base, flat blue-green leaves in two ranks, a winter’s rest, then a bulb of new cloves under purple-streaked skins and a curling scape.

layer.label: 6 · Roots
layer.note: grown for what they swell below the soil: roots, tubers, bulbs

stages.name: Clove
stages.note: A clove planted in autumn, pointed end up, five centimetres down.

stages.name: Rooting
stages.note: White roots break from the flat base plate.

stages.name: Shoot
stages.note: A green shoot pushes up out of the clove’s tip.

stages.name: First leaves
stages.note: Flat blue-green leaves in two ranks, before the frost.

stages.name: Winter
stages.note: It rests through the cold, roots growing on.

stages.name: Spring growth
stages.note: New leaves fast in the lengthening days; the old clove is used up.

stages.name: Bulbing
stages.note: The base swells: a bulb is forming, splitting inside into cloves.

stages.name: Scape
stages.note: The flower stalk shoots up from the middle and curls in a loop.

stages.name: Swelling
stages.note: The bulb fattens, its papery skins streaked purple; the lower leaves brown.

stages.name: Harvest
stages.note: Half the leaves brown: lift the bulb and dry it.

ginger@1.label: Ginger
ginger@1.note: From a piece of rhizome: reed-like stems a metre high, two ranks of narrow leaves; below the soil, the hand branching into knobbly fingers, pink where each stem rises.

layer.label: 6 · Roots
layer.note: grown for what they swell below the soil: roots, tubers, bulbs

stages.name: Seed piece
stages.note: A plump piece of rhizome with two or three eyes, laid flat five centimetres down in warm, moist soil.

stages.name: Sprouting
stages.note: The eyes swell, pink and green-tipped; white roots go down from the underside.

stages.name: Shoot
stages.note: A pointed shoot, rolled tight, breaks the soil.

stages.name: First leaves
stages.note: A reed-like stem unrolls its leaves in two ranks, one to each side in turn.

stages.name: Clump
stages.note: New knobs on the rhizome, each sending up a stem of its own.

stages.name: Reeds
stages.note: A clump of leafy stems a metre high; below, the hand branching into fingers.

stages.name: Young fingers
stages.note: New fingers of rhizome fill out under the soil, pink where each stem rises.

stages.name: Baby ginger
stages.note: Tender, thin-skinned, pink-tipped: dug now, it is mild and needs no peeling.

stages.name: Swelling
stages.note: The fingers fatten and their skins toughen to tan, ringed with scars.

stages.name: Harvest
stages.note: The leaves yellow and fall over: lift the clump, keep a hand back to plant again.

jerusalem-artichoke@1.label: Jerusalem artichoke
jerusalem-artichoke@1.note: From a knobbly tuber, hairy stems nearly three metres tall with rough leaves and little yellow sunflowers; below, a nest of new tubers, dug all winter.

layer.label: 6 · Roots
layer.note: grown for what they swell below the soil: roots, tubers, bulbs

stages.name: Tuber
stages.note: A knobbly tuber the size of a hen’s egg, ten centimetres down in early spring.

stages.name: Sprouting
stages.note: White shoots from its eyes, roots below.

stages.name: Shoots
stages.note: Stout hairy shoots break the soil, rough leaves in pairs.

stages.name: Leafy
stages.note: Stems knee-high, broad, rough, dark green leaves.

stages.name: Tall
stages.note: Stems two metres, the leaves alternate higher up; under the soil, white stolons run out.

stages.name: Towering
stages.note: A thicket nearly three metres tall — a windbreak and a screen; the stolon tips start to swell.

stages.name: Flowering
stages.note: Small yellow sunflowers at the tops in September, the bees and hoverflies at them.

stages.name: Tubers
stages.note: Under the soil, a nest of knobbly tubers filling out.

stages.name: Frosted
stages.note: The first frosts blacken the leaves; the stems stand brown and the tubers grow sweet.

stages.name: Digging
stages.note: Dug as needed all winter; any tuber missed comes up again next spring.

horseradish@1.label: Horseradish
horseradish@1.note: From a root cutting, a clump of big wavy, long-stalked leaves and white flower sprays; below, a white taproot thick as a wrist that brings the tears.

layer.label: 6 · Roots
layer.note: grown for what they swell below the soil: roots, tubers, bulbs

stages.name: Root cutting
stages.note: A pencil-thick piece of side root (a thong), planted slanting in spring, its top end up.

stages.name: Sprouting
stages.note: Buds break at its top; white roots from all along it.

stages.name: First leaves
stages.note: A tuft of narrow leaves, the earliest deeply cut like combs.

stages.name: Rosette
stages.note: Long-stalked oblong leaves, glossy, their edges wavy and crinkled.

stages.name: Clump
stages.note: Leaves sixty centimetres and more, standing up in a dark clump; gone back to the crown in winter.

stages.name: Second spring
stages.note: Back from the crown, bigger: a clump near a metre high.

stages.name: Flowering
stages.note: Branched stems rise a metre with clouds of small white four-petalled flowers, honey-scented.

stages.name: Summer
stages.note: The flowers fall (it hardly ever sets seed); the leaves at their biggest.

stages.name: Root thickening
stages.note: In autumn the taproot fills out, white as a parsnip and thick as a wrist.

stages.name: Lifting
stages.note: Lifted after the frosts: grated, it brings the tears. The side roots are kept to replant — and any piece left in the soil grows again.

cucumber@1.label: Cucumber
cucumber@1.note: From a flat seed to a vine on its stake: lobed rough leaves, coiling tendrils, yellow flowers, warted cucumbers hanging.

layer.label: 7 · Climbers
layer.note: vines that climb the trees, the stakes and the wires

stages.name: Seed
stages.note: A flat cream seed, a centimetre long, two centimetres down in warm soil.

stages.name: Germination
stages.note: The radicle dives; the hypocotyl arches up through the soil, its peg holding the coat back.

stages.name: Seed leaves
stages.note: Two oblong cotyledons open on a stem a few centimetres high; the taproot already branches.

stages.name: True leaves
stages.note: The first rough, lobed true leaves; the vine begins between the seed leaves.

stages.name: Vining
stages.note: Half a metre of vine, a leaf at each node, tendrils finding the stake and coiling round it.

stages.name: Flowering
stages.note: Yellow flowers in the leaf axils: clusters of male ones, and females with a tiny cucumber behind.

stages.name: Fruit set
stages.note: Pollinated, the tiny prickly cucumbers behind the female flowers start to swell; the flowers shrivel.

stages.name: Swelling
stages.note: The first cucumbers hang a hand long, pale-striped and spiny; more flowers open higher up.

stages.name: Filling out
stages.note: Cucumbers down the vine, dark green and warted; the lowest leaves begin to yellow.

stages.name: Harvest
stages.note: Full-sized cucumbers ready to cut, young ones following behind; the roots spread wide and shallow.

grape@1.label: Red grape
grape@1.note: From a pip to a vine trained on its post and wire: a woody trunk, two arms, green shoots with five-lobed leaves and tendrils, bunches turning red berry by berry.

layer.label: 7 · Climbers
layer.note: vines that climb the trees, the stakes and the wires

stages.name: Pip
stages.note: A small pear-shaped pip, chilled through the winter, a centimetre down.

stages.name: Germination
stages.note: The radicle goes down, the hook comes up.

stages.name: Seedling
stages.note: Two oval seed leaves and the first lobed, toothed true leaves.

stages.name: First summer
stages.note: A slender vine climbing its stake, a tendril opposite every leaf.

stages.name: Trained
stages.note: Pruned to one woody trunk up the post and two arms along the wire, short spurs on the arms.

stages.name: Flowering
stages.note: Green shoots up between the catch wires; tiny green flowers in clusters shed their caps.

stages.name: Fruit set
stages.note: Clusters of hard little green berries set, opposite the third and fourth leaves.

stages.name: Green berries
stages.note: The bunches swell and close up, berry pressed to berry, still green and sour.

stages.name: Véraison
stages.note: Berry by berry they soften and turn: green, pink, red, the bunch speckled.

stages.name: Ripe
stages.note: Deep red-purple bunches dusted with bloom, sweet: the harvest.

passion-fruit@1.label: Passion fruit
passion-fruit@1.note: A vine up its stake and along a wire, shoots hanging like a curtain; three-lobed leaves, astonishing flowers with a crown of purple-and-white filaments, round fruit turning purple and wrinkling.

layer.label: 7 · Climbers
layer.note: vines that climb the trees, the stakes and the wires

stages.name: Seed
stages.note: A small black pitted seed from the pulp, a centimetre down.

stages.name: Germination
stages.note: The radicle goes down, the hook comes up.

stages.name: Seed leaves
stages.note: Two oval seed leaves, then simple oval true leaves.

stages.name: Climbing
stages.note: A slender vine up its stake, tendrils grabbing, the leaves now three-lobed.

stages.name: On the wire
stages.note: Over the top and along the wire both ways; shoots hang down like a curtain.

stages.name: Flowering
stages.note: Extraordinary flowers on the hanging shoots: white petals, a crown of purple-and-white filaments, the stigmas on a column.

stages.name: Fruit set
stages.note: Pollinated, each flower leaves a small round green fruit.

stages.name: Green fruit
stages.note: Glossy green balls the size of an egg, hanging on their stalks.

stages.name: Colouring
stages.note: They darken to purple.

stages.name: Ripe
stages.note: Deep purple, wrinkling as they ripen; they drop when ready.

beans@1.label: Runner bean
beans@1.note: The bean stays below; the shoot winds anticlockwise up its cane, leaves of three, sprays of scarlet (or white) flowers, long green pods hanging in bunches.

layer.label: 7 · Climbers
layer.note: vines that climb the trees, the stakes and the wires

stages.name: Bean
stages.note: A big kidney-shaped bean, mottled purple and black, five centimetres down in warm soil after the last frost.

stages.name: Germination
stages.note: The root goes down; a hooked shoot pushes up — the bean itself, its two halves full of food, stays below.

stages.name: First leaves
stages.note: A pair of simple, heart-shaped leaves, opposite each other, at the top of the shoot.

stages.name: Trifoliate
stages.note: The first leaf of three leaflets; the tip already circling, feeling for something to climb.

stages.name: Climbing
stages.note: Winding anticlockwise up its cane, a leaf of three at every node.

stages.name: Flowering
stages.note: Long sprays of pea-like flowers from the leaf axils, opening from the bottom up, bumblebees at them.

stages.name: Pods set
stages.note: Most flowers drop; behind a few, thin green pods.

stages.name: Young pods
stages.note: Slender pods a hand long — the best for picking, before the beans show.

stages.name: Long pods
stages.note: Rough green pods twenty and thirty centimetres long, hanging in bunches: pick them and more come.

stages.name: Picking
stages.note: Picking every few days; a pod left on swells lumpy with its beans and yellows, to keep for seed.

kiwiberry@1.label: Hardy kiwi
kiwiberry@1.note: A vigorous vine twining up its post and along the bar, rounded leaves on red stalks hanging in a curtain, nodding white flowers, and clusters of smooth green kiwiberries the size of grapes.

layer.label: 7 · Climbers
layer.note: vines that climb the trees, the stakes and the wires

stages.name: Seed
stages.note: A tiny dark seed from a kiwiberry, chilled through the winter, sown on the surface.

stages.name: Germination
stages.note: A root goes down, a thread of a shoot comes up.

stages.name: Seed leaves
stages.note: Two small oval seed leaves, then rounded hairy ones.

stages.name: First shoots
stages.note: A young vine finds its post and twines up it, anticlockwise.

stages.name: On the bar
stages.note: Over the top and along the bar both ways, a woody trunk twisted round the post, shoots hanging down.

stages.name: Flowering
stages.note: Nodding white flowers with dark anthers in the axils of the new shoots’ lowest leaves, scented of lily of the valley.

stages.name: Fruit set
stages.note: The petals drop; little hairless green fruit hang in the leaf axils.

stages.name: Green fruit
stages.note: Clusters of grape-sized, smooth green fruit along the base of every shoot.

stages.name: Swelling
stages.note: The fruit fill out and soften, a bronze blush on the sunny side.

stages.name: Ripe
stages.note: Soft, smooth, sweet kiwiberries to eat skin and all, hanging under a curtain of leaves.

hop@1.label: Hop
hop@1.note: From its rhizome, three bines twining clockwise up a pole four and a half metres high, rough lobed leaves in pairs, side arms hung with papery cones ripening golden.

layer.label: 7 · Climbers
layer.note: vines that climb the trees, the stakes and the wires

stages.name: Rhizome
stages.note: A piece of last year’s rhizome with its buds, a hand down at the foot of its pole, in early spring.

stages.name: Shoots
stages.note: Red-flushed shoots push up; most are cut and eaten like asparagus, the three strongest kept.

stages.name: Training
stages.note: The three bines find the pole and wind clockwise up it, their stems rough with hooked hairs that grip.

stages.name: Climbing
stages.note: Up to a hand’s breadth a day, a pair of rough, lobed leaves at every node.

stages.name: Halfway
stages.note: Over two metres up the pole; the lowest leaves stripped to let the air through.

stages.name: Over the top
stages.note: At the top of the pole and over; side arms grow from the leaf axils in the upper half.

stages.name: Burrs
stages.note: The female flowers: soft, spiky green burrs clustered on the side arms.

stages.name: Green cones
stages.note: The burrs swell into papery green cones, bract over bract.

stages.name: Ripening
stages.note: The cones dry and rustle, yellow lupulin dust inside smelling of beer and resin.

stages.name: Harvest
stages.note: Golden cones picked; the bines cut down and the leaves yellowing; in spring it comes again from the rhizome.

wine-cap@1.label: Wine cap
wine-cap@1.note: The food forest’s mushroom: spawn in a bed of wood chips, white rhizomorphs binding the chips and running into the soil, then a troop of wine-red caps on white stems.

layer.label: 8 · Fungi
layer.note: the mycelium in the soil and the wood, and the mushrooms it fruits

stages.name: Spawn
stages.note: Spawn — grain or sawdust grown through with mycelium — mixed into a bed of fresh hardwood chips.

stages.name: Running
stages.note: White threads run out from the spawn through the damp chips.

stages.name: Colonising
stages.note: Thick white cords, rhizomorphs, bind the chips together and reach down into the soil.

stages.name: Colonised
stages.note: The bed is white through; the mycelium feeds the soil and the plants around it.

stages.name: Pinning
stages.note: After rain: tiny wine-red knobs push up out of the chips.

stages.name: Buttons
stages.note: Round wine-red buttons on stout white stems.

stages.name: Opening
stages.note: The caps open, their veil tearing into a ring with ridged edges.

stages.name: Mature
stages.note: Big burgundy caps a hand across, their gills turning purple-grey with spores.

stages.name: Fading
stages.note: The caps fade to tan as they age; pick them young.

stages.name: Next flush
stages.note: The bed rests and flushes again, as long as the chips last: top it up each year.

shiitake@1.label: Shiitake
shiitake@1.note: An oak log plugged with spawn and sealed with wax; months of colonising, a cold soak, then brown flecked caps breaking from the bark, again for years.

layer.label: 8 · Fungi
layer.note: the mycelium in the soil and the wood, and the mushrooms it fruits

stages.name: Plugging
stages.note: A fresh-cut oak log, drilled in a diamond pattern; plugs of spawn tapped in and sealed with wax.

stages.name: Running
stages.note: The mycelium runs out from each plug through the wood, unseen.

stages.name: Colonising
stages.note: White mottling creeps over the cut ends.

stages.name: Colonised
stages.note: The ends are white through: the log is ready to fruit.

stages.name: Shocked
stages.note: Soaked a day in cold water to wake it.

stages.name: Pinning
stages.note: Small knobs push through cracks in the bark.

stages.name: Buttons
stages.note: Brown buttons with a white-fringed rim.

stages.name: Opening
stages.note: The caps open, brown with pale flecks, their gills cream.

stages.name: Mature
stages.note: Caps a hand across, edges just beginning to flatten: pick now.

stages.name: Resting
stages.note: The log rests a couple of months, then fruits again — for four or five years.

oyster@1.label: Oyster mushroom
oyster@1.note: A standing beech log; after the first cold rains, clusters of grey-blue fans that spread into overlapping shelves, their white gills running down the stem.

layer.label: 8 · Fungi
layer.note: the mycelium in the soil and the wood, and the mushrooms it fruits

stages.name: Plugging
stages.note: A beech log, drilled and plugged with oyster spawn, stood on end in the shade.

stages.name: Running
stages.note: The mycelium runs through the wood.

stages.name: Colonising
stages.note: White mycelium shows on the cut top.

stages.name: Colonised
stages.note: Colonised through: it fruits when the autumn turns cool and wet.

stages.name: Cold snap
stages.note: The first cold rains: the trigger.

stages.name: Pinning
stages.note: Clusters of tiny grey knobs burst from the bark.

stages.name: Clusters
stages.note: Tight clusters of little grey-blue fans.

stages.name: Shelves
stages.note: The fans spread into overlapping shelves, white gills running down their short stems.

stages.name: Mature
stages.note: Shelves of grey caps a hand across: cut the whole cluster.

stages.name: Spent
stages.note: Old caps curl and pale; the log rests until the next cold spell.
